Everyone’s skin is different, that product that makes one person on Instagram look amazing might trigger an irritation or allergy on your skin.   It’s not just advanced products that you run a risk, it can happen with natural ingredients and the most basic products. You can experience irritation from something as simple as a cleanser or toner but that doesn’t make the product bad. (Check my previous video on contact dermatitis, so you see what it can look like). There are two types of contact dermatitis.  1 Irritant contact dermatitis, which happens quickly—within minutes to hours of exposure.  2 Allergic contact dermatitis, which takes repeated exposure to the product and days to develop—at least 4 days.  These reactions come with reddening, dryness, itching, rashes, peeling, burning, blistering, and swelling. Make sure you patch test all new skincare products. Patch test products on a small area such as the side of the neck, underside of jaw or inner arm and do this for at least 4 days to determine if a delayed reaction (delayed hypersensitivity reaction) develops.  Once you have confirmation that the product or ingredient doesn’t irritate your skin, you should be safe to apply it to your face or body. PS: You can also experience contact dermatitis once you stop using questionable skincare products, triple action creams, bleaching creams, and steroids. This can happen for a while until your skin normalizes. This is part of steroid withdrawal syndrome but that is a topic for another day. This is a picture taken from the front of the inside of the nose, showing a defect on the nasal septum. Nasal septal perforations are essentially a hole/defect in the cartilage and/or bone that separates the right and left side of your nose. They are commonly due to trauma (including nose picking!), surgery and substance abuse and can lead to symptoms such as crusting, blocked nose, whistling, and bleeding. There are lots of cool ways to repair them, but a common treatment is with a septal button and emollients to prevent the symptoms as repairs can fail. #nose #ent #allergy #otolaryngology #otolaryngologist #nosejob #nosesurgery #septalperforation #septorhinoplasty #septoplasty #nosepicker #nosepicking #nosepick

Here is a good example of a #postop adhesion - this is where scar tissue in the nose fuses together, usually after trauma (commonly surgery & irritant substances) to both sides of a nasal cavity. These adhesions can lead to failure of surgery to improve nasal airway by closing up the passages we have opened up. Thankfully this one was too high up in the nose to cause problems. #ENT #otolaryngology #otolaryngologist #allergy #infection #FESS #sinus #sinuscare #sinusitis #surgery #nose #nosesurgery #sinussurgery #sinussurgeryrecovery #sinusinfection

🎥 In this video, Alex explains what tears are and why we need them.   👨🏻‍🔬 Alex Ionides, Consultant Ophthalmic Surgeon at Moorfields Eye Hospital (and co-founder at MTHK).   👁️👁️ Despite being incredibly thin, our tear film is made up of three essential layers that all play a part in keeping our eyes healthy.   1. MUCOUS (MUCIN) LAYER Closest to your eyes is the mucin (mucous) layer. It sits atop the cornea, the clear part of the front of the eye, and provides a foundation for the other tear layers to maintain the right shape and stay in place.   2. WATERY (AQUEOUS) LAYER In the middle is the aqueous (watery) layer, which provides moisture, oxygen and other nutrients to the cornea affectionately called the ‘windscreen’ of the eye. It helps to wash away anything that gets into the eye, such as dirt, so the front of your eye stays smooth (so it can see and focus properly).   3. OILY (LIPID) LAYER The top layer of tears furthest from your eye is the lipid (oily) layer. It floats on the tears and seals in the moisture of the aqueous layer underneath, making sure your tears are spreading over your eye correctly and stopping them from evaporating too quickly.   #MTHK #EyeHealth #optician #optometrist #dryeye #eyesight #dryeyerelief #dryeyedisease #opthalmologist #lizearlewellbeing #eye #eyehealthtips #vision #dryeyes #dryeyesyndrome #menopausesymptoms #Lutein #menopause #hayfever #eyedrops #eyedoctor

yesterday we went to the docs as blue still seemed flared, we got given aptmil pepti 2 yesterday too try for a trail of 2 weeks, Blue instantly after one bottle started going red, hives around his face, unsettled, could hear his tummy rumbling and he puked up atleast 2/3 oz 20mins after. Took me 3 hours to settle him he was exhausted and just fell to sleep on me, 6oclock come he woke for a feed. I decided too try him with another just in case it was all in my head, half a bottle of 7oz he had and threw it back up again. My gut was telling me it’s definitely allergy related & not to give it a trail for two weeks. I immediately took him off, & back onto Alfamino because I had two tins spare. Within giving him 7oz guzzled it down, he settled straight away. We both ended up sleeping majorly of the night! And woke up to blue not as bad as late last night. He’s been on Alfamino all day and he’s slot more settled & comfortable catching up on his beauty sleep! Dairy free free with Double E - Chicken and Mushroom Filo Pie 🤍✨🍴 1. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees  2. Cook the chicken - season chicken with salt, pepper and rosemary (or herbs of your choice) air fry, or oven bake until cooked 3. Whilst the chicken is cooking, prep your veg if choice. We have chosen to do mushroom and spinach 4. Fry the mushrooms until cooked and add the spinach until it’s wilted  5. Add the chicken stock with 400ml of boiling water to the cooked vegetables  6. Once the chicken is cooked, put onto a plate and shred  7. Add the chicken into the chicken stock and veg mix 8. Add 2 tsp of Dijon mustard 9. Add 90ml of dairy free plant cream, if you want to add more you can  10. Mix together  11. Add 2 tbsp of plain flour to thicken the sauce, feel free to add more or less depending on the consistency  12. Once all cooked and at the consistency you’re happy with, transfer to an oven dish 13. Get the filo pastry (6 sheets) cut the sheets into half, and scrunch into loose balls and place them on top of the filling 14. Spray the pastry with oil of your choice (we use fry light)  15. Cook for 30 minutes or until the sauce is bubbling hot and the filo is crisp and golden  16. Serve with your veg and sides of choice, we have gone for mash and broccoli Let us know if you try the recipe it’s sooo yum! Part 4: BREASTFEEDING & BABY ECZEMA ELIMINATION DIET I think one of the hardest things about having a young child is this need to give up a lot of yourself. The same goes for doing an elimination diet.  Because food (proteins?) can go into your breast milk, your child can still have a reaction which means as a breastfeeding Mum, to do the elimination diet you have to eat exactly what your baby or toddler does. The hardest thing is on top of the sleep deprivation and giving all you have to this tiny human, when it seems like everything else is taken away, (even if it’s for your child, it can be really hard) food is a last comfort. But then you start to restrict and you ‘miss out’ on treats. I’ll be honest there are some days you wish this wasn’t for you, but then you look at your child and know you’d do anything for them. They are your highest value, short term change in your diet is a small price to pay for figuring out what’s causing your child’s symptoms.  . #eatallergysafe #glutenfree #nutfree #paleo #allergy #eliminationdiet #babyeczema #ketovore #mumlife #mumlife #carnivore #eczema #firsttimemum #attachmentparenting #gentleparenting #pregnancy #postpartumrecovery #toddlerlife #motherhood

Dairy Free Easy Chicken Gyros 🍴 Ingredients: -450g chicken -2tsp oregano -300g frozen chips -4 Greek style flat bread -Dairy free sour cream dip (we got ours from Tesco) -Dairy free feta cheese (we got ours from Lidl) -A few spoonfuls of chutney of your choice (we used the tomato and chilli one from Tesco) -half a cucumber -a few handfuls of rocket  Instructions: 1. Preheat the oven to 190 degrees 2. Cut chicken into small strips  3. Add chicken strips to an oven dish and sprinkle over some oregano along with salt & pepper 4. Spray the chicken with some fry light or oil of your choice  5. Cook the chicken for roughly 30 minutes or until cooked through 6. Add your oven chips (or homemade) to a baking tray, season with salt & pepper and cook for roughly 30 minutes depending on the time needed  7. Whilst the chicken and chips are cooking, diced the cucumber and feta into small cubes 8. Put the flatbreads onto a baking tray and add to the oven when there is 2 minutes left on the timer  9. Once the flatbreads are warm, place them on a plate. Add a sauce base (we used dairy free sour cream but you can use whatever you prefer). Then add the chutney, cucumber, feta and rocket 10. Place 3-4 strips of chicken on top, along with a a handful of chips 11. This #epic  #romance is a #must-read for all #fans of #Paolo Nutini's music. Fred, twenty-three years old and Paolo's biggest fan, suffers from a #raredisease, #MCAS, short for Mast Cell Activation Syndrome. It makes her so #reactive that merely going out of the house already puts her in danger of suffering an #anaphylactic shock. When her parents decide to move her from #Berlin back to her provincial hometown #Marburg in the heart of #Germany to look after her in the final stages of her illness, Fred feels as if her #life is over. But with the help of her parents, her sister and her cousin small changes begin to happen. She manages to finish her degree, rekindles her close #friendship with her cousin, and finds out what she wants to do with the rest of her (probably short) life. To make her #life-long #dream come true of seeing #PaoloNutini on stage she risks going on a #journey to #Milan with her #oxygen  tank in the boot of the car, her cousin Timo, with whom she is secretly in #love, her sister Liesel and her sister’s partner Alina. On the way, they stop over in Luzerne where Fred for the first time meets someone like her, an MCAS.From there she feels a hope rekindling that she might have a life that is worth living, worth fighting for, after all. #bookclub  #passion #hope and #loss, #suffering and #endurance, about a #family  #mortality. #Bookworm #Bookish #booktok #lovestory #novel #tomance #romantic #forbiddenlove #allergyfree #reading #audiobook #relaxing #audible  #booklover #LGBT #comedy #black #humour #irony #sarcasm #contemporary #literature #women #anaphylaxis #foodallergies #foodallergy  #histamine #histamineintolerance #MCS #MCAS #mastcell #epipen #paolonutini     #mcas #mastcellactivationsyndrome #perfumeallergy #mcas #mastcell #mastcellactivation #paolonutinilive #anaphylacticshock #allergy #lgbtq #lgbt #lgbt🌈 #

Dairy free Truffle Bacon Mac & Cheese 🍴 Makes enough for 3-4 people Ingredients: -300g bacon (lardons or rashers) -350g macaroni pasta  -200ml dairy free creme fraiche or cream (we used @Oatly oat fraiche) -150g dairy free grated cheese (we used @cathedral_city_uk plant based cheese) -350ml chicken stock -1tsp truffle oil -100g dairy free butter (we used Flora dairy free) -85g plain flour  -Breadcrumbs for topping -Olive Oil 1. If you have gone for bacon rashers, pre-heat your grill to around 220 degrees. On a baking tray, cover with foil and lay out the bacon. Grill bacon until crispy. Once cooked, let the bacon cool. On a chopping board, cut up the bacon into small pieces and set aside.  2. If you have gone for bacon lardons, in a frying pan add a splash of oil and fry until crispy.  Once cooked, set aside.  3. In a large saucepan, fill with water and add the macaroni with a tsp of salt, cook for around 12 minutes or until cooked. 4. In a medium saucepan, add in the butter to melt, once melted add the flour to form a roux paste. 5. Gradually stir in the chicken stock and the crème fraiche. Whisk until the sauce has thickened and to remove any lumps.  6. Add in the grated cheese and whisk again. Add in the truffle oil and stir. Once all the cheese has melted, stir in the bacon.  7. Drain the cooked macaroni and transfer to an ovenproof dish. 8. Pour the sauce over the macaroni and mix together. 9. Pre-heat the grill again to around 200 degrees. 10. In a small bowl add the breadcrumbs and a splash of oil. Mix this together and sprinkle over the macaroni. You can also add some pepper to season if you wish.  11. Grill the macaroni until the topping is crispy. 12. Serve and enjoy! So this is the most common question i am being asked since starting our health testing......❤️ What's the difference between an intolerance and an allergy? So in a nutshell..... A food allergy occurs when the immune system reacts to a food which is usually harmless 🙀 Food intolerance occurs when the body has a chemical reaction to eating a particular food or drink 😷  A true food allergy affects the immune system. Even small amounts of the offending food can trigger a range of symptoms, which can be severe or life-threatening. In contrast, a food intolerance often affects only the digestive system and causes less serious symptoms. So basically, if your symptoms are: - Abdominal (belly) pain. - Diarrhea. - Gas and bloating - Headaches or migraines - Heartburn - Nausea - Upset stomach You are more likely to have an intolerance and i would recommend our food intolerance test, if your symptoms are any of the below i would recommend taking our food and environmental allergy test. - Tingling or itching in the mouth. - A raised, itchy red rash (urticarial) – in some cases, - - The skin can turn red and itchy, but without a raised rash - Swelling of the face, mouth (angioedema), throat or other areas of the body - Difficulty swallowing - Wheezing or shortness of breath Pop us a DM to order your health test for next day UK delivery (if ordered before 3pm) 😜  #intolerance #glutenfree #food #life #allergy #lifestyle #healthy #dairyfree #health #healthyliving #wheatfree #foodsensitivity #vegan #healthylifestyle #wellbeing #foodallergies #sensitivity #insta #instahealth #intolerancetest  #intolerancetesting #sensitivities  #heathlylife #fingerpricktest #dreambodynutrition

Fermented red onion and sumac are both known for their potential health benefits, particularly for individuals suffering from hay fever. Fermented red onion is rich in antioxidants and flavonoids that can help to reduce inflammation in the body, including the inflammation associated with hay fever. Additionally, the fermentation process may enhance the onion's anti-inflammatory properties.  In Chinese medicine, sumac is believed to have a number of benefits for individuals suffering from allergies. Sumac, or "Qin Jiao", is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties and is commonly used to reduce swelling and inflammation in the body. It is also believed to have antiallergic properties and may be used to alleviate symptoms such as itching, sneezing, and runny nose. Sumac is also believed to have a positive effect on the respiratory system and may be used to treat conditions such as asthma and bronchitis. It’s also  believed to have a strengthening effect on the immune system, which may help individuals with allergies to better fight off allergens and prevent future allergic reactions. You can easily make this fermented sumac onion and add to your salads, preferably daily to see benefits. Slice  2 big 1 small red onion. Put in a glass jar or airtight storage container. Add 10tbsp of olive oil, 10tbsp of organic apple cider vinegar, bit of salt( preferably  salt without iodine), lots of sumac. Close the lid and leave in the kitchen cabinet for one day. Host a Dairy Free Dinner Party with us 🌟  A slightly different post but this weekend we organised a dairy free dinner party for Em’s birthday and we wanted to share how we did it and the menu and share so inspo for anyone planning to do the same in the future. You do not have to go out if you have an allergy or don’t feel safe, you can bring the meal to the comfort of your own home. The dairy free menu consisted of: Starter - prawn pil pil served with crusty ciabatta bread  Main - chicken breast in a white wine, cream and mushroom sauce, served with truffle potato gratin and asparagus and Tenderstem broccoli  Dessert - white chocolate and passion fruit cheesecake  We promise to get the recipes of Em’s mum soon, or the ones she adapted for the party 🤤 We were really lucky that Em’s mum made all the food for us and helped serve it, but you could even do courses that you prep and just heat up on the day if you want to do it yourself, or if you trust your friends each bring a course.  We got the balloon arch from @Amazon , the name signs from @Etsy  and most of the table decoration is from @Dunelm  ✨ We made 2 cocktails - a Hugo and a pornstar martini which we knew were all allergy free and then we made a pina colada and strawberry daiquiri mocktail which again were so yum! We then also had Prosecco and wine which again had all been checked before serving. From someone with an allergy eating out is so scary and filled with anxiety, so it is so lovely bringing the restaurant to your house and knowing the food is all safe. #SlurpeeRun Hay Fever Support: Spring has sprung, the days are getting longer, daffodils are blooming and many of us are hoping for a beautiful summer. But for the millions of hay fever sufferers in the UK, the season of sneezing, runny noses and itchy eyes is just around the corner, and for many, this range of debilitating symptoms can have a very real impact on everyday life. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, or “hay fever” occurs when your body identifies pollen as a threat and launches an inappropriate immune response to this normally harmless substance. While hay fever frequently begins at a young age, it can affect both adults and children, affecting an estimated 10-15% of children and 26% of adults in the UK – equating to around 16 million of us – with a 2020 study suggesting that the figure could actually be as high as 49% of adults.1,2 Symptoms can arrive with tree pollens as early as March and continue through the summer months with grass pollens. When pollens come into contact with the nostrils, eyes, or throat of an individual with sensitivity, the immune system produces the antibody IgE (immunoglobulin E). IgE then binds to white blood cells, which causes the release of pro-inflammatory histamine, resulting in sneezing, itchy and watery eyes, swelling and inflammation of the nasal passages and an increase in mucous production. If you suspect you may have Hayfever and want to confirm it, we have blood tests available to test environmental allergies. Preparation is key, and ensuing a great level of these key nutrients, supporting gut health and following an anti-inflammatory, low histamine diet should be implemented as early as possible before symptoms start to appear. Host a Dairy Free Dinner Party with us 🌟  A slightly different post but this weekend we organised a dairy free dinner party for Em’s birthday and we wanted to share how we did it and the menu and share so inspo for anyone planning to do the same in the future. You do not have to go out if you have an allergy or don’t feel safe, you can bring the meal to the comfort of your own home. The dairy free menu consisted of: Starter - prawn pil pil served with crusty ciabatta bread  Main - chicken breast in a white wine, cream and mushroom sauce, served with truffle potato gratin and asparagus and Tenderstem broccoli  Dessert - white chocolate and passion fruit cheesecake  We promise to get the recipes of Em’s mum soon, or the ones she adapted for the party 🤤 We were really lucky that Em’s mum made all the food for us and helped serve it, but you could even do courses that you prep and just heat up on the day if you want to do it yourself, or if you trust your friends each bring a course.  We got the balloon arch from @Amazon , the name signs from @Etsy  and most of the table decoration is from @Dunelm  ✨ We made 2 cocktails - a Hugo and a pornstar martini which we knew were all allergy free and then we made a pina colada and strawberry daiquiri mocktail which again were so yum! We then also had Prosecco and wine which again had all been checked before serving. From someone with an allergy eating out is so scary and filled with anxiety, so it is so lovely bringing the restaurant to your house and knowing the food is all safe. The first year of my baby's life was so difficult. She spent most of her days scratching, bleeding and crying. The eczema covered her entire body and it was awful to watch. There were some natural products we tried that did help soothe the skin a little but nothing helped in the long term. The doctors also prescribed 4 different steroids and emollients but it was no use. We made sure she only wore cotton, kept her moisturised, kept allergens away as much as possible, changed washing detergent.  I was constantly worried about her getting an infection and things came to a head when I was driving one day. I looked in the rear view mirror and noticed her in the car seat with blood all round her mouth. She had bitten off a layer of the skin on her hand where it was so itchy. I was desperate to help my baby and was recommended a group on Facebook called Dr Aron (I know this sounds like an 'ad' but it's really not!). Getting an appointment with him was the best thing I ever did for my daughter as her skin changed almost immediately. If anyone else has a child with severe eczema and nothing is working, have a look into it. Unfortunately the treatments aren't available on the NHS but the money I paid privately was so worth it. Dairy Free @Zizzi Pollo Picante Pasta 🍴 Our dairy free take of the Zizzi Pollo Picsnte Pasta! This is the most delicious and crowd pleasing pasta you can make. Its also super easy and one of our favourite pasta dishes ever! (Serves 2-3) Ingredients: -Chicken breast per person  -250ml dairy free cream (we used Elmlea plant cream) -250g cherry or plum tomatoes  -160g of pasta (we used Casarecce pasta from @Tesco) -100g spinach  -3-4 tsp of @BELAZU (Bel-uh-zoo) rose harissa paste (you can add more or less depending on how much spice you can handle) -optional dairy free parmasean to serve (we used Lidl vegan parmasean) Method: 1. Cut up your chicken in to small pieces. Season the chicken and cook in the air fryer or oven until cooked through (roughly 20 mimutes) 2. Whilst the chicken is cooking, place the pasta in a large saucepan and cook for around 12 minutes or until cooked. 3. Cut the tomatoes in half and add to a large saucepan or dish. Cook the tomatoes until softened. 4. Add the cream and the harissa paste and mix until the sauce has changed colour. 5. Add the spinach to the creamy sauce and mix in until wilted. Meanwhile drain the pasta.  6. Add the cooked chicken and the pasta to the dish and mix all together. 7. Leave to simmer for a few minutes. 8. Serve and enjoy!  Let us know if you try it! The first year of my baby's life was so difficult. She spent most of her days scratching, bleeding and crying. The eczema covered her entire body and it was awful to watch. There were some natural products we tried that did help soothe the skin a little but nothing helped in the long term. The doctors also prescribed 4 different steroids and emollients but it was no use. We made sure she only wore cotton, kept her moisturised, kept allergens away as much as possible, changed washing detergent.  I was constantly worried about her getting an infection and things came to a head when I was driving one day. I looked in the rear view mirror and noticed her in the car seat with blood all round her mouth. She had bitten off a layer of the skin on her hand where it was so itchy. I was desperate to help my baby and was recommended a group on Facebook called Dr Aron (I know this sounds like an 'ad' but it's really not!). Getting an appointment with him was the best thing I ever did for my daughter as her skin changed almost immediately. If anyone else has a child with severe eczema and nothing is working, have a look into it. Unfortunately the treatments aren't available on the NHS but the money I paid privately was so worth it. They deal with patients worldwide too. My daughters most recent allergy test shows she is no longer allergic to wheat, peanut or cows milk which is fantastic! #eczema #allergies #allergy #eczemaawareness #eczematok

Summer glow look for all us hay fever sufferers!  My eyes are always running during this time of year. I often sneeze too. This season tends to be all allergy suffers worst time.  Use water resistant/ waterproof eye makeup (like my liquid liner, mascara & lash glue) If possible stay away from liquid foundations, especially in the day time as it can cause more irritation. Applying a balm around your nostrils can help to catch some of the pollen in the air before it triggers those annoying hayfever symptoms like congestion, sneezing and a runny nose.   Here's how I make my hayfever nose balm:   Add 1 tsp of beeswax and 2 tsp virgin coconut oil to a beaker or heat proof container and melt them.   Once the beeswax and coconut oil are melted, add 2 drops of lavender, 1 drop of lemon and 1 drop of peppermint essential oil and mix to combine.    Pour the mixture into a suitable container to set at room temperature.    Once it's fully set, it's ready to use. It's been unlike anything I've experienced before and is testing me in ways I never thought it would. The constant itchiness, stinging in my eyes, and throat bumps are making my days quite challenging. To add to it, the heatwave in the UK is compounding the issue. Wearing a mask, while offering some respite, is a task in itself given the hot weather. However, it does ease my symptoms a bit, allowing me to breathe a little more comfortably. I've been investing in various remedies, trying to find something, anything that can provide me some relief. One such investment is the air purifier you see in this video attached to the post. I've had it for two days now, and although I haven't noticed a significant difference yet, I remain hopeful. I'm planning to give it a fair trial for a week before deciding its effectiveness. This year's hay fever season has been incredibly tough for me, waking up with swollen eyes and struggling to breathe in the middle of the night. But remember, everyone's experience can vary greatly. If you're experiencing a similar battle, know that you're not alone and stay strong. I will be sharing more tips and tricks soon on how to cope with this challenging hay fever season. Let's navigate this tough time together, and here's hoping none of you have to deal with such troublesome allergies. Some beauty clinics offer an injection called Kenalog which is a form of corticosteroid that contains triamcinolone which suppresses the immune system’s reaction to pollen. There are alternative treatments you can trial before going down this route, also discuss with your own dr if you are still considering this treatment for your hay fever. Note that I recommend that everyone has a full health analysis before taking supplements, because not all will apply to you. There are so many factors to think about when working with allergies and it’s not easy to tackle hayfever and other allergy mediated disorders, especially if you’ve had it a long time. Using the functional medicine approach can certainly help reduce or mitigate symptoms of hayfever, but it takes work and time! Hayfever Injections are a NO ❌ from me! 💐 Around 1 in 4 of us suffer from Hayfever and symptoms can have quite a big effect on our day to day lives so it is understandable why we start to look for alternative forms of treatment  💉 Hayfever injections are steroid injections that go by the name Kenalog  🚫 Kenalog is not licensed in the UK to treat hayfever and it is no longer offered by the NHS due to safety concerns. The UK government have also banned all social media advertising for this reason also 💊 If you are struggling with hayfever try nasal sprays, nasal rinses, oral antihistamines and allergy eye drops.  🌳 Non-medical measures include: - Staying indoors on high pollen days - Wearing sunglasses and/or masks to stop the pollen entering your nose or eyes - Shake out clothes/bedding on a daily basis - Wash your hair often as pollen gets trapped in there - Avoid alcohol as it causes a histamine release which could worsen symptoms  - Try eating local honey 1-2 months before hayfever season starts  Good luck and stay safe!  www.elegance-aesthetics.com  #eleganceaestheticsdrazb #eleganceazb #drazb #hayfever #hayfeverhacks #aesthetics @AZB

Death by hayfever 🥹 I remember I got an F in my geography test when I was 14, because my hayfever was so bad 🥹  I’ve had it as long as I remember, but it’s gotten better as I’ve gotten older and learnt about how the immune system works. Most years I don’t really suffer too badly, but this year, hayfever seems to be back with a vengeance especially after a month of overindulging on deliciously difficult to digest foods in Hong Kong and Japan, and then experiencing 3 days of urticaria in reaction to I still don’t know what 🤦🏻‍♀️😃👍🏼 allergy results from the NHS are taking FOR-EVER! (Oh well, when in Rome) As a result, I suspect my gut is pretty leaky. Intestinal hyperpermeability AKA leaky gut is where the gut lining, where you absorb your food but also keep unwanted material like allergens out, gets compromised.  As most of your immune system also sits there so dysregulation of the gut, microbiome and gut lining can impact your immune response. Therefore optimising your digestive health helps to support your immune system. Hayfever is an atopic disorder meaning that it’s allergy leaning. Simply put, the immune system needs to be balanced and regulated, and this depends on the bacteria in your body, your inflammatory response and the learning it did as you grew up (I.e. were we exposed to enough germs? Were our environments oversanitised? Were we vaccinated more than necessary? Were we given too many antibiotics? Is there a family history of immune dysregulation and allergy?). The immune system is dynamic and it’s ever changing and adapting, which means it is technically possible to reduce your hayfever symptoms, if not, remove them completely. However, it’s not an easy feat and you can regain allergies later in life due to stress, poor diet/lifestyle, poor recovery and sleep. Don’t let hay fever ruin your summer! Researchers suggest there is a link between hayfever and your gut microbiome. Go figure! Health does start in the gut after all. People with hay fever often have a less diverse gut microbiome, resulting in higher levels of inflammation, less breakdown of histamine, and ultimately hayfever. Take care of your gut health first and foremost, by eating a varied, whole-food diet and taking a histamine-specific probiotic like Histaminex by @Seeking.Health (not an ad, and no affiliation). And then do this: 🍯 Take local honey builds pollen tolerance 🍃 Take quercetin - nature's antihistamine 💊 Take DAO enzyme or kidney supps to help with the breakdown of histamine (see my amazon store for the one I use) 🚫 Avoid high-histamine foods 🏠 Invest in an air filter for your home Plus, there are certain genetic variants that can determine your susceptibility to hay fever and how bad you’re going to get it. It’s worth doing a test with a company like @Omnos.me to find out. What’s your go-to hayfever hack? PMS & Hayfever 🤧  Much like the symptoms of PMS, the effects of histamine on the body are inflammatory. Inflammation could be what is driving your PMS and hayfever symptoms.  Some studies suggest that women who experience histamine intolerance are more likely to suffer from PMS. On top of this, excess histamine (which is what gives us hayfever complaints) has been found to release more oestrogen (and too much oestrogen in relation to our other hormones is what drives a lot of PMS symptoms) - creating a vicious cycle of symptoms.  What can you do? An anti-inflammatory diet is an important step. How I introduced peanut to my daughter! As a Paediatric Dietitian with a special interest in food allergy, I KNOW that introducing allergens can be really worrying for parents. I thought I’d share top tips and info for peanut introduction- an allergen parents are often VERY nervous about Remember - proactive and timely introduction of allergens, especially egg and peanut are now well evidenced to help support allergy prevention! Avoid delaying introduction of these foods if you can Top tips ✔️ Never give whole peanuts, use a no added salt or sugar SMOOTH peanut butter or well ground unsalted peanuts. Peanut butter can still pose a choking risk so if its thick and/or tacky then dilute with a little warm water or milk ✔️Offer on a day when your baby is well ✔️ Offer in foods your baby has had before and always do one allergen at a time (A had already had wheat and milk) ✔️ Start small - i used 1/4 teaspoon here but you can start smaller if nervous. Aim to increase to around 1 tsp  ✔️ Peanut reactions are typically immedate type responses (rather than delayed allergy), so I’d expect symptoms usually within minutes but a maximum of 2 hours later Any weaning or allergy questions? How I introduced peanut to my daughter! As a Paediatric Dietitian with a special interest in food allergy, I KNOW that introducing allergens can be really worrying for parents. I thought I’d share top tips and info for peanut introduction- an allergen parents are often VERY nervous about Remember - proactive and timely introduction of allergens, especially egg and peanut are now well evidenced to help support allergy prevention! Avoid delaying introduction of these foods if you can Top tips ✔️ Never give whole peanuts, use a no added salt or sugar SMOOTH peanut butter or well ground unsalted peanuts. Peanut butter can still pose a choking risk so if its thick and/or tacky then dilute with a little warm water or milk ✔️Offer on a day when your baby is well ✔️ Offer in foods your baby has had before and always do one allergen at a time (A had already had wheat and milk) ✔️ Start small - i used 1/4 teaspoon here but you can start smaller if nervous. Aim to increase to around 1 tsp  ✔️ Peanut reactions are typically immedate type responses (rather than delayed allergy), so I’d expect symptoms usually within minutes but a maximum of 2 hours later Any weaning or allergy questions? Protect your bed Your bed is the biggest hotspot in your home for dust mites they have everything they need, plenty of food, moisture, warmth and a place to lay their eggs. At night, you are spending 8 hours nuzzled into their favorite place. This prolonged exposure is the reason you may often wake up with reduced mental clarity, reduced breathing and skin issues. This is why it must be addressed first.   - Dust Mite Protectors - Protectors are the best way to reduce the dust mites ability to live and breed in your bed. This prevents dust mites creating a home inside your duvet, pillows and mattress as they are unable to penetrate the barriers. The dust mites must now live on the surface sheets of your bed which you can regularly wash to remove dust mites and their proteins. 2. Replace all carpeted floors Now that you have protected your bed, you need to focus on removing any carpets from your property. Your carpet may not be as warm or humid as your bed, but if your house is covered in carpet, you are allowing them to actively breed. Your footsteps will disturb the allergens found in your carpet, which you will breathe in. - Hard flooring throughout your property - ensure the new hard flooring is easy to clean and you minimize gaps to prevent dust building in those areas. - Cannot replace your carpet? - unfortunately replacing your carpet may not be an option due to cost or your do not own your property. The next best steps you can do are regularly steam clean your carpet, regularly vacuum and as a last resort apply a dust mite spray to your carpet 3. visit https://dustmitetreatment.com/blogs/news/1-protect-your-bed for full information         #eczema #asthma #rhinitis #sinusitis #dustmite  #allergy #dustmitealeergy #foodallergy #inflammation

Are you someone with ADHD who also has allergies, eczema, hay fever or asthma or suffers from hives, rhinitis or mast cell activation?   There seems to be a link emerging between a high histamine state and ADHD, and this is something we are seeing in our test results at NatureDoc more and more frequently - like very high histidine markers and these genetic tests showing poor histamine breakdown in people who have ADHD.   Interestingly two key nutrients which help to break down excess histamine in the body are zinc and vitamin B6 and these are well established to be found to be deficient in people with ADHD. They help to balance the nervous system and help with regulating dopamine and norepinephrine. When you have severe allergies, travelling can be both exciting and daunting. It’s essential to take specific precautions to ensure your safety while on the go. One of the most crucial steps is ensuring that your EpiPens, which are lifesaving devices designed to counter severe allergic reactions, are in optimal condition. First and foremost, checking the expiry date of your EpiPen is paramount. Expired EpiPens may not deliver the required dose of adrenaline, which is essential for treating anaphylaxis. Using an expired EpiPen could be ineffective in addressing a severe allergic reaction, putting your life at risk. Moreover, the physical condition of your EpiPen matters. Discolouration or a broken seal can be indicators of compromised devices. Discolouration might suggest that the medication has deteriorated or been exposed to unfavourable conditions, rendering it less effective or potentially harmful. EpiPens will turn yellow when they discolour, like the one on the right in the video. A broken seal could lead to contamination, making the EpiPen unsafe for use. Furthermore, packing two EpiPens in your hand luggage is a prudent practice. Allergic reactions can escalate rapidly, and having a backup EpiPen is a safety net in case the first one fails to work correctly or if more than one dose is needed to control the reaction. Lastly, keeping your EpiPens in your hand luggage ensures accessibility during your journey. In an emergency, you may not have immediate access to your checked baggage, making it essential to have your EpiPens within reach. Allergenic Foods Can Be Introduced Early: In the past, parents were often advised to delay introducing common allergenic foods like peanuts, eggs, and shellfish. However, recent research suggests that introducing these foods early, around 6 months of age, can actually reduce the risk of allergies. Always consult your pediatrician before introducing allergenic foods, especially if there's a family history of allergies. Don't Introduce Cow's Milk Too Early: Cow's milk should not be introduced as a primary drink until after your baby's first birthday. Before then, breast milk or formula should be the main source of nutrition. Iron-Rich Foods Are Vital for Brain Development: After the age of six months, your baby's iron stores from birth start to deplete. Introduce iron-rich foods like fortified cereals, lean meats, and dark green vegetables to support healthy brain development and prevent iron-deficiency anemia. #babiesoftiktok #babyfood #weaning #weaningbaby #allergy #iron #milk #parentingtips #6monthsold

*Sensitive Content Warning* The following content may be distressing or sensitive in nature. It contains images or discussions related to a severe allergic reaction and hives, resulting from allergies. Viewer discretion is advised. This week is anaphylaxis awareness week, and this year it’s all about empowering people with the right knowledge and building confidence to help safely manage serious allergies. It’s common to believe that anaphylaxis is an immediate life threatening reaction, but it can also actually occur up to 2-3 hours after an exposure! A few years ago, I ate out at a Turkish restaurant and triple checked the food didn’t contain nuts. After a few bites, I knew straight away that the food was full of nuts and I started to feel unwell. My mouth started to swell, my pulse started to race, I had my epipen at the ready but this didn’t progress into anaphylaxis, so I assumed it would be ok. Hours later, I got into bed that evening still feeling unwell, but my whole body had broken out into hives and I started to experience shortness of breath. I called 111 and they instructed me to go to hospital immediately in case this progressed into anaphylaxis. I spent the evening in hospital on a drip, under observation, and luckily this didn’t turn into anaphylaxis. Knowledge and preparedness are our greatest allies when it comes to managing severe allergies. My story shared here underscores the unpredictability of allergic reactions. I was lucky, but it could’ve been a life threatening reaction for others. The importance of remaining vigilant and seeking immediate medical attention when faced with unexpected symptoms cannot be overstated. If like me, you suffer from life threatening allergies, always carry epipens and check them regularly to ensure that they are in date, not discoloured and the seals are intact! #anaphylaxis #allergy #nutallergy #allergicreaction #funnymemes

Many people living with severe allergies are at risk of experiencing anaphylaxis if they come into contact with an allergen. Anaphylaxis, many of you will know is a life-threatening condition that can come on suddenly and worsen very quickly, typically requiring the use of an adrenaline injector pen and urgent medical attention. A new survey has found that there is a real lack of awareness by patients about the proper use of their adrenaline pens and it also found that a quarter don’t always carry their pens with them when they are out and about. Less than half said that they would feel confident using one in a medical emergency - which is equally worrying. This is why ready2reactuk is such an important public awareness campaign. Share it as wide as you can to help educate patients, carers and wider society about the importance of when and how to use their adrenaline pens correctly. To learn more about severe allergies and how to stay safe, please visit www.ready2react.co.uk *ready2reactuk is endorsed by a multidisciplinary steering committee made up of allergy specialists, healthcare professionals, charities, schools, and patients, striving to educate the public about allergies, anaphylaxis, and the use of adrenaline pens.#makeallergyhistory  #ready2reactuk #natashasfoundation #natashaallergyreasearchfoundation #anaphylaxis #allergy #allergicreaction

#stitch with @SHIV Anaphylaxis is a severe allergic reaction that can occur rapidly after exposure to an allergen.  Keep an eye out for symptoms like a new rash, such as hives, itchiness, abdominal pain and eye watering. Later, more severe symptoms could occur like  difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, tongue or throat, and a sudden drop in blood pressure. These can occur within seconds to 30 minutes of exposure - and exposure isn't always eating something, it can be touch or sometimes even in the air too.  If you or someone else shows these signs, act swiftly. If one is prescribed then give adrenaline via an epipen. (Remember orange to the thigh, blue to the sky) and seek emergency medical attention. This is for every mum out there wondering if things would get any better. I'm one of you! From running your child to therapy, hospital visits, praying for some breakthrough or just holding out hoping that it would get better some day. - I feel you! To the mom researching non stop to help her child live a full and happy independent life, I applaud you! 👏  To the dad who looks at his child when other kids are rehearsing football and he can't, I understand you. Don't worry it might not be football for him but another talent yet untapped.  To the mom who can't take her child to social events for the fear of him humping on the ground due to hormonal imbalances brought on by puberty - it would be alright and this too will pass. I see you! To the dad still grieving for the child he hoped and envisaged when he heard the words from his wife 'we're pregnant' don't lose heart, he is the child given to you by God just not what you expected. I  hear you! To the mum who just got her son's diagnosis and it's not looking good -  don't lose hope. I know how you feel! To that mum and dad, hoping, wishing and praying to hear their child call them 'mum or dad' or just talk one day. This Just Ruined Coffee 🤢 #allergy. In the realm of food production, it might surprise many to know that there are acceptable levels of insects allowed in various food products. Regulatory bodies and food safety standards acknowledge that complete elimination of insects from the food supply chain is practically challenging. Here's an insight into this aspect of food safety: Insect Contamination Standards: Regulatory agencies, such as the FDA and other international bodies, have established permissible levels of insect parts in certain foods, recognizing that a complete absence is impractical. Unavoidable Contaminants: Insects can inadvertently find their way into food during cultivation, harvesting, processing, or transportation, making it challenging to eliminate them entirely. Protein Source: In some cultures, insects are intentionally consumed as a protein source, highlighting cultural variations in acceptable food practices. Quality Assurance Measures: Food manufacturers implement rigorous quality assurance measures to minimize insect contamination, but some level of acceptance is built into standards. Nutritional Considerations: Insects are rich in protein, fiber, and other nutrients, and intentional inclusion in certain food products is being explored for nutritional benefits. Risk Assessment: Regulatory agencies conduct risk assessments to determine the potential health risks associated with the consumption of insects in food, ensuring that acceptable levels are within safe limits. Common Examples: Products like canned fruits, grains, and chocolate are among those where some level of insect contamination may be deemed acceptable within established guidelines. #FoodSafety #InsectConsumption #RegulatoryStandards #CulturalDiversity #ProteinSource #SustainableFood #FoodQuality #NutritionalBenefits #GlobalFoodSupply #CulinaryPractices #ConsumerAwareness #FoodRegulations #InsectProtein #SustainableNutrition #AcceptableLevels #CulturalDiversityInFood #Entomophagy #FoodProduction #SustainableDiet #HealthAndWellness #FoodSecurity #fyp #fypシ #medicine

Did you know that mould growth can trigger asthma and allergies, affecting the air we breathe at home?  Let's take a closer look and learn how to create mould-free environments for better respiratory health. Why Mould Matters: Mould releases spores into the air, which, when inhaled, can be problematic for individuals with asthma and allergies.  It's crucial to address and prevent mould growth to ensure a safe and healthy living space. Tips to Tackle Mould: 1. Ventilation: Keep your home well-ventilated to reduce moisture, a key factor for mould growth. 2. Regular Cleaning: Wipe down surfaces regularly, especially in moisture-prone areas like bathrooms and kitchens. 3. Fix Leaks Promptly: Address water leaks promptly to prevent dampness and mould development. 4. Allergy-induced asthma, often known as allergic asthma, is a condition where asthma symptoms are triggered by exposure to allergens.  Let’s explore what it is and how you can manage it for better respiratory health. What is Allergy-Induced Asthma? In allergic asthma, the airways become sensitive to certain allergens, such as pollen, pet dander, mould, or dust mites. When exposed to these triggers, it can lead to asthma symptoms like wheezing, shortness of breath, and coughing. Managing Allergy-Induced Asthma: 1. Identify Triggers: Work with your healthcare provider to identify specific allergens triggering your asthma. 2. Create an Allergen-Free Zone: Minimise exposure to allergens at home by keeping living spaces clean and well-ventilated. 3. Consult Your Asthma Nurse or GP: If you suspect allergy-induced asthma, seek guidance from your asthma nurse or GP for proper diagnosis and management. 🌟 Support Our Mission: Your support helps us raise awareness and provide resources for those managing allergy-induced asthma.  Contribute to initiatives promoting asthma and allergy awareness at https://www.justgiving.com/asthma-allergyfoundation. Every donation makes a difference!  💬 Contact Us for Assistance: Have questions or need assistance in managing allergy-induced asthma? Reach out to us at info@asthmaandallergy.org.uk.  We’re here to help you breathe easier.  Remember, if you suspect you have allergy-induced asthma, don’t hesitate to consult with your healthcare professional for personalised advice.  Together, we can navigate the journey to better respiratory health. #AllergyAsthmaAwareness #AAF #Asthaawareness #allergy #Inhaler #breatheeasy

1. Myth A little but won't hurt, just let him have a chocolate button. Anyone heard this?  Fact Yes, it probably will and giving that chocolate button could cause tummy upset, skin reaction and could lead to anaphylaxis in more severe cases 2 Myth Lactose free milk will help with symptoms  Fact Lactose free milk still has milk protein contained. It's the lactose that has been removed (the sugar). If your little one has a milk allergy then Lactose free milk or following a lactose free diet won't help symptoms. Lactose intolerance is very rare in babies. Secondary lactose intolerance can happen after a tummy bug or antibiotics but isn't a milk protein allergy. 3.  Myth Allergy tests are needed to diagnose milk allergy Fact Not always. Allergy tests can be completed to help to diagnose IgE (immediate) milk allergy but just having a positive test result doesn't automatically mean an allergy to milk. Its so important that a clear history is taken.  Delayed allergy will be diagnosed via elimination and likely reintroduction. This is the same with other allergies and we have something called cross reactivity so it is important that a qualified professional takes a full history alongside the allergy test. Testing for allergies can be confusing 🤯 🌟If your little one has a delayed allergic reaction, symptoms between 2-72 hours after having a food, then you should be supported for elimination and reintroduction  🌟If your little ones symptoms are immediate (straight away up to 2 hours later) then IgE blood tests, skin prick tests or in some cases oral food challenges may be complete.  ❗It's so important however that you speak to a health professional (a Dietitian like me) and give a full history. Some babies can have a mixed reaction or multiple allergies and we need to get the diagnosis and treatment correct.  It might not be safe to reintroduce or it may be fine. Every baby is unique. Replying to @Kyra Kate  Like all medicines, cetirizine can cause side effects, although not everyone gets them. Common side effects The most common side effect of cetirizine is feeling sleepy and tired. This happens in more than 1 in 10 people. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist if this side effect bothers you or does not go away. Other common side effects of cetirizine happen in more than 1 in 100 people. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist if these side effects bother you or do not go away:     headaches     dry mouth     feeling sick (nausea)     feeling dizzy     diarrhoea     sore throat     sneezing or blocked and runny nose Children are more likely to get diarrhoea, sneezing or a blocked and runny nose than adults. Serious side effects It's rare to have a serious side effect with cetirizine. Chuffed with this! I've not made bread and butter pudding before but it's on the nursery menu this Wednesday! So I've made a version that my little one can enjoy and I'll send it with @Alpro  custard 🙂 I'm hoping he likes being able to see that he's eating the same as his little friends... it may even improve his eating. At the moment my LO is mainly spoon fed but i am trying to encourage independent feeding 🙂 I spent ages trailing the Internet looking for a recipe but in the end just did a hybrid version and it worked 🥰  I used:  1/2 loaf schar best of both bread cut up into cubes  3 cups of alrpo soya milk 1 tsp cinnamon  1/4 cup melted vegan spread  1/4 cup sugar  1/4 cup golden syrup (the recipes I saw were suggesting maple so depends what you like, I only had GS in).  2 mini boxes of raisens. Super simple too... put the bread cubed into the dish, mixed everything else up in a bowl and then poured it over before mixing it and baking in the oven for 35mins 🥰 Yum!  #mumlife #food #homemade #homebaking #freefrom #weaning #weaningjourney #toddlersoftiktok #toddlerlife #dairyfree #nurseryfood #nursery #allergy #baby #wheatfree #glutenfree #mumsoftiktok #eggfree #easycook #fyp #fy #allergyawareness #pudding #breadpudding

I had my first severe allergic reaction when I was just five years old. My best friend’s mum offered to make me peanut butter on toast - and even though I asked for toast with just butter, I knew something was wrong after just one bite. The same knife had been used on both pieces of toast, and the traces of peanut butter was enough to give me hives, swelling, difficulty breathing. After being poked, pricked, and tested, I left the hospital with my life changed - and two adrenaline pens in my hand. Fast forward about twenty years and I’ve learned to live with my allergy, although: - with stories of ‘avoidable’ deaths constantly popping up on the news... - issues getting hold of (and keeping) a set of adrenaline pens... - and the stigma, lack of awareness and misinformation... It hasn’t been easy. In 2020 I went to university to study industrial design, and that’s when I came up with the idea to create something “just like a defibrillator, but for allergies”. A year after graduating in the peak of COVID, I met James.  We both went all-in on the business and quickly started ramping things up - raising our first round of investment, securing a pharmaceutical partner, and running a successful pilot phase with our first prototype. Simon then joined us to help build out our software platform, and Jonny to help boost our sales efforts and growth. Suddenly 1 became 4, and it was clear this wasn’t just a university project anymore. At the start of 2023, it was finally time for us to officially launch - and that’s when things got really crazy. Just over a year since then, and we’ve: - Installed Kitts in over 300 schools across the UK - Provided 150,000 students with access to emergency allergy treatment - Had 4,000 staff members complete CPD-accredited allergy training But the most amazing thing that’s happened? Our Kitts have actually been used in an emergency to treat someone’s life-threatening allergic reaction. Twice. This all started with my initial diagnosis. But it ends with an Anaphylaxis Kitt being every single defibrillator’s next-door neighbour. #allergy #founder #startup #founderstory #medtech #health #epipen #school #nurse #safety #firstaid

Natasha's Law is a food labelling law, but some businesses have been using it incorrectly for their own purposes. A number of you have contacted us and shared your experiences. Below are some examples of what you have told us: ◇ A cinema attendant stating that it is not possible to take your own food into the theatre because of Natasha's Law. ◇ A trampoline park chain stating that visitors, including those with food allergies, are only allowed to purchase and eat food in their restaurants (we checked and they aren’t free from any allergens) because of Natasha's Law. ◇ A number of Soft Play Centres that don't allow any food to be brought into their premises, even if it's for a child with food allergies. You can only purchase food from their cafes (that have allergen ingredients in their food) because of Natasha's Law. ◇ One mother asked a restaurant to heat up a bottle of milk formula in the microwave because her baby was hungry and crying, and she was told that it was not possible because of Natasha's Law. To be clear, Natasha's Law protects people with food allergies who rely on the transparency of clear food labelling on pre-packed foods. Had sesame seeds (a top 14 allergen) been listed on the ingredient label of the pre-packed baguette that Natasha ate, she would never have eaten it and would be alive today. Natasha's Law is her legacy and has established new food labelling standards for food businesses. It's implementation has highlighted the battle people face against the growing epidemic of food allergies in the UK. If it is being used for any other purposes, such as in the examples described above, it is most likely that it is being misused for their gain.  #allergic #foodallergies #anaphylaxis #natashaslaw #allergy #allergens

The Food standards agency (FSA) has launched an awareness campaign for the public to understand #food allergen risks that exist in vegan foods. There is a concern that people with food allergies to milk, eggs, fish, crustaceans or molluscs are at risk from serious allergic reactions to foods that have been labelled as ‘vegan.’ Research worryingly shows that many people with these food allergies are buying #vegan and plant-based food and wrongly assuming that they are safe for them to eat. There is in fact a serious risk of #allergen cross contamination because vegan food is not always safe for people with these allergies, due to manufacturing and preparation processes. The campaign also highlights the differences between a vegan or plant-based food label, and a free-from food label. Vegan food labels are used to support a lifestyle choice, and though they don’t intentionally contain products of animal origin, they could still be prepared in manufacturing areas alongside products such as egg, #milk #fish #crustaceans or #molluscs - whereas free-from foods are not. The #FSA state that a ‘free-from’ food label, guarantees the product doesn’t contain the specified allergen. To use this label, food businesses must follow strict processes to ensure the allergen isn’t present. However, these rules don’t apply to vegan or #plantbased products, which means that there is always a #risk of allergen cross-contamination. So #donttaketherisk – check the label.

Natasha's Law is a food labelling law, but some businesses have been using it incorrectly for their own purposes. A number of you have contacted us and shared your experiences. Below are some examples of what you have told us: ◇ A cinema attendant stating that it is not possible to take your own food into the theatre because of Natasha's Law. ◇ A trampoline park chain stating that visitors, including those with food allergies, are only allowed to purchase and eat food in their restaurants (we checked and they aren’t free from any allergens) because of Natasha's Law. ◇ A number of Soft Play Centres that don't allow any food to be brought into their premises, even if it's for a child with food allergies. You can only purchase food from their cafes (that have allergen ingredients in their food) because of Natasha's Law. ◇ One mother asked a restaurant to heat up a bottle of milk formula in the microwave because her baby was hungry and crying, and she was told that it was not possible because of Natasha's Law. To be clear, Natasha's Law protects people with food allergies who rely on the transparency of clear food labelling on pre-packed foods. Had sesame seeds (a top 14 allergen) been listed on the ingredient label of the pre-packed baguette that Natasha ate, she would never have eaten it and would be alive today. Natasha's Law is her legacy and has established new food labelling standards for food businesses. It's implementation has highlighted the battle people face against the growing epidemic of food allergies in the UK. If it is being used for any other purposes, such as in the examples described above, it is most likely that it is being misused for their gain.  #allergic #foodallergies #anaphylaxis #natashaslaw #allergy #allergens

This is Hiding In Your Mattress? 🤢 #vacuum. Dust mites, microscopic creatures that thrive in indoor environments, are a common trigger for allergies. Although dust mites themselves are not the direct cause of allergic reactions, it is their fecal matter and body fragments that contain proteins known to induce allergic responses in sensitive individuals. Here's a detailed description of what in dust mite poop triggers allergies: Allergen Proteins: Dust mite droppings contain specific proteins that are potent allergens, capable of triggering immune responses in susceptible individuals. The primary allergens associated with dust mite feces are Der p 1 and Der p 2 (from Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus) and Der f 1 and Der f 2 (from Dermatophagoides farinae). These proteins are highly stable and can remain allergenic even after the dust mites have died. Airborne Particles: Dust mite feces are microscopic in size and can become airborne when disturbed, such as during activities like dusting, vacuuming, or even simply walking on carpets or sitting on upholstered furniture. When inhaled, these airborne particles can penetrate deep into the respiratory system, where they come into contact with mucous membranes and trigger allergic reactions. Immune Response Activation: Upon exposure to dust mite allergens, the immune system of allergic individuals recognizes these foreign proteins as harmful invaders and mounts an immune response to neutralize them. This immune response involves the release of histamine and other inflammatory substances, leading to typical allergy symptoms such as sneezing, coughing, nasal congestion, itchy eyes, and skin rashes. Sensitization: Prolonged or repeated exposure to dust mite allergens can lead to sensitization, wherein the immune system becomes increasingly reactive to these specific allergens over time. Sensitized individuals may experience more severe or frequent allergic reactions upon subsequent exposures to dust mite feces, making avoidance measures crucial for symptom management. #allergy

Should She Have Used Her EpiPen? #allergy. An adrenaline auto-injector, commonly known as an Epipen, is a life-saving device used to administer a dose of adrenaline (epinephrine) in cases of severe allergic reactions, such as anaphylaxis. While adrenaline can rapidly reverse the symptoms of an allergic reaction and prevent potentially life-threatening complications, its administration via an Epipen may also lead to certain side effects. Understanding these side effects is crucial for individuals who may need to use an Epipen, as well as for healthcare providers and caregivers who may administer the medication. Here's a detailed exploration of the potential side effects associated with an adrenaline Epipen injection: Increased Heart Rate (Tachycardia): Adrenaline stimulates the heart, leading to an increase in heart rate. While this can be beneficial in an emergency situation to improve circulation and oxygen delivery, it may cause palpitations or a sensation of rapid or irregular heartbeat. Elevated Blood Pressure (Hypertension): Adrenaline constricts blood vessels, which can lead to a temporary increase in blood pressure. Individuals with pre-existing hypertension or cardiovascular conditions may be at greater risk of experiencing elevated blood pressure as a side effect of an adrenaline injection. Nervousness and Anxiety: Adrenaline is known for its stimulatory effects on the central nervous system. As a result, some individuals may experience feelings of nervousness, restlessness, or anxiety after receiving an adrenaline injection. Tremors: Adrenaline can cause involuntary muscle tremors, particularly in the hands or fingers. These tremors are typically mild and transient but may be noticeable to the individual receiving the injection. Headache: Some individuals may experience headaches as a side effect of adrenaline administration. This may be due to the vasoconstrictive effects of adrenaline, which can affect blood flow to the brain. Nausea and Vomiting: Adrenaline can stimulate the gastrointestinal system, leading to nausea or vomiting in some individuals. These symptoms are usually mild and may resolve on their own without specific treatment. #adrenaline

5 Symptoms You Should Never Ignore - Hay Fever Edition 🌼 Severe Sneezing Fits: While occasional sneezing is common, persistent and severe sneezing fits, especially when accompanied by a runny or blocked nose, can significantly impact your daily life and indicate unmanaged hay fever. Intense Itchy, Watery Eyes: One of the hallmark symptoms of hay fever, intense itching and watering of the eyes can not only be uncomfortable but also interfere with your vision and daily activities. Difficulty Breathing or Wheezing: If you find yourself struggling to breathe, or if you're wheezing, especially during high pollen counts, it could be a sign that your hay fever is exacerbating asthma or other respiratory issues. Loss of Smell and Taste: Ongoing nasal congestion and inflammation can lead to a temporary loss of smell and taste, diminishing your enjoyment of food and drinks, and affecting your overall quality of life. Persistent Headaches and Fatigue: Chronic hay fever can lead to persistent headaches and a feeling of fatigue due to poor quality sleep and the constant battle against symptoms, impacting your concentration and energy levels. Recognizing and addressing these symptoms with appropriate treatments and lifestyle adjustments can help manage hay fever effectively, allowing you to enjoy the seasons without discomfort. If these symptoms persist, consulting with a healthcare provider is crucial for finding relief and preventing complications. #hayfever  #hayfeversymptoms  #generalhealth  #knowyourbody  #medicineexplained

Spring has sprung🪻🌸🌷 And with that comes the ever looming threat of a scratchy throat, sneezes and a runny nose.  For voice users who suffer with hayfever and allergies it can be a tricky time to navigate.  Here are 6 useful tips to help you keep your voice happy during this period: 🌷 Drink plenty of water - when suffering with allergies and hayfever, hydration is super important, especially if you are taking allergy medication. These medications can dry out the vocal tract and sinuses, so to keep your voice happy keep your hydration up sipping little and often throughout the day.  🪻Steam and nebulise - topical hydration is key to keeping your vocal folds happy. When allergies strike your vocal folds can become inflamed and unhappy, leading to a scratchy throat and hoarse voice. Steaming or nebulising will help to soothe the vocal tract and give the vocal folds the much needed hydration they deserve.  Remember to use saline solution for a nebuliser and boiling water (let it cool for a few minutes before use) for steaming.  🌸 Nasal/Sinus rinse - great for helping to clear any excess mucous in the nasal cavity and clear away any unwanted irritants that might be sitting at the back of your nose. We use the NeilMed sinus rinses. Available online or in most chemists. 🌷 Saline nasal spray - super handy for keeping the nasal cavity hydrated and clearing out excess mucous when you aren’t able to do a full nasal rinse. These are different from decongestant nasal sprays, which, whilst being helpful in moments of congestion, can also be very drying to your voice. If you’re looking for a saline nasal spray, make sure it only contains either saline or salt water. These are available at most chemists.  🪻SOVT exercises - therapeutic exercises are your friend when your vocal folds are inflamed. Wide straws in water, puffy cheeks or lip trills are a great way to help gently warm up/cool down your voice. The back pressure will help to reduce the inflammation and ease your voice into a comfortable place in order to speak or sing.  🌸 Pacing/Vocal naps - if your voice is struggling due to allergies, be kind to your voice and allow time to rest. Adding in regular, short vocal naps throughout the day will help to conserve your vocal battery and help to reduce fatigue. If you have a busy day, pace your voice use, being aware of overdoing it and taking from tomorrows vocal battery. #edinburghvoicecare #vocalmassagescotland #voicehealth #singingteacher #vocalcoach #vocalhealthworkshops #voice #allergies #hayfever #evc #hydrate

Atleast 1 in 5 of us experience hay-fever symptoms, and while it can be irritating to live with, pregnancy can make treating and reducing some of the symptoms that little bit harder. 💊Whilst there are hay-fever medications that can still be taken during pregnancy (you can ask more about these at your local pharmacy), some of the supermarket tablets / any which cause drowsiness do need to be avoided, and any medications / sprays containing steroids are also off limits when expecting.  🌻So what can we do to ease daily symptoms? 🫖Drinking Chamomile tea can help to ease symptoms as it contains anti-inflammatory properties. Alternatively you can make a strong bowl of the tea and inhale the steam to cleanse the lungs and sinuses. 🍯It’s thought that eating a spoon of local honey each day can help to build up a natural immunity against your local pollens. Try adding a spoonful to your tea above for added benefits!  🏠Close windows while you sleep to limit the amount of pollen in the house. 🕶️Wear wraparound sunglasses to protect your eyes. 🧖🏼‍♀️Wash your hands and face regularly, particularly when you get home, or use hand and face wipes while you’re out and about to remove any pollen off you. 🙅🏻‍♀️Dab a few dots of barrier balm around the edge of each nostril and under each eye to trap pollen before it enters. 👃🏽Rinse the inside of your nose with an over-the-counter saline solution to wash out pollen, avoiding any that contain steroids if pregnant. 👚Avoid hanging clothes outside to dry on high pollen count days, so they don’t come into contact with pollen.  👁️Place a cold compress on itchy eyes to cool them. As tempting as it can be to rub your eyes, doing this will only irritate them further.  🍃If hay-fever has caused congestion and your nose to become blocked, inhale our Breathe Easy pulse point rollerball from your wrists to cool any inflammation and irritation while out and about. Alternatively if you’re at home, spritz the Breathe Easy room spray around your living space to open the airways back up, or spray onto a cloth or tissue and inhale. #hayfever #naturalremedies #hayfeverinpregnancy #aromatherapy #essentialoils #pureessentialoils #natural

What Causes Hay Fever? Pollen: The most common trigger for hay fever is pollen from trees, grasses, and weeds. When pollen particles enter the nose, throat, or eyes, they can cause an allergic reaction in sensitive individuals. Mould Spores: Airborne spores from moulds found both outdoors and indoors can trigger hay fever symptoms. These spores can be present all year round but may peak during warm and humid conditions. Dust Mites: These tiny creatures found in household dust can cause symptoms of hay fever. While they are present indoors, their waste products can be inhaled, leading to allergic reactions. Animal Dander: Proteins found in the skin flakes, urine, and saliva of furry pets such as cats and dogs can cause hay fever. It's not the fur itself but these proteins that trigger the symptoms. Environmental Factors: Changes in weather, such as wind which can carry pollen and spores over long distances, and pollution, which can exacerbate the sensitivity of the airways to allergens, also play significant roles in triggering hay fever symptoms. Understanding these triggers is crucial for managing hay fever, as avoidance and appropriate treatment can significantly reduce symptoms and improve quality of life. #hayfever  #hayfevercheck  #health  #knowyourbody  #medicineexplained

Which Hay Fever Treatment Is Right For YOU? 🌼 Use This, Not That - Hay Fever Edition Fexofenadine (Telfast) or Cetirizine: For long-lasting relief without drowsiness, opt for Fexofenadine, also known as Telfast. Prefer a more readily available option? Cetirizine can be your go-to for quick allergy relief. Pirinase Nasal Spray or Clarinaze Nasal Spray: If you're battling both nasal congestion and other allergy symptoms, Pirinase offers a versatile solution. For targeted relief from nasal congestion and allergens, Clarinaze is your best bet. Sodium Cromoglicate 2% Eye Drops or Opticrom Eye Drops: Both are great for itchy, watery eyes caused by hay fever. Sodium Cromoglicate offers fast relief, while Opticrom is ideal for those who prefer a well-established brand. Sterimar Nasal Spray or Beconase Nasal Spray: For a natural, non-medicated option to clear and moisturise nasal passages, choose Sterimar. Need something stronger for persistent nasal symptoms? Beconase Nasal Spray can provide more potent relief. Clarityn Tablets or Piriteze Tablets: Clarityn is perfect for day-long relief from hay fever symptoms without drowsiness. For a different option that also promises 24-hour relief and is effective against a range of allergies, Piriteze is a strong contender. Sneezing, coughing ,runny nose or itchy watery eyes? Yes it's the season for Hay Fever again!! 😬 & Although you cannot cure it, there are things you can do and medicines you can take to ease your symptoms 🤧 Speak to a pharmacist if you have hay fever who can suggest the best treatments to help with symptoms, such as oral antihistamine,eye drops or nasal sprays. Speak to GP, if your symptoms are getting worse or your symptoms do not improve after taking medicines from the pharmacy. Your GP can prescribe you combined nasal sprays 👃 (combined intranasal antihistamine and corticosteroid such as Dymista) or oral steroid treatment 💊 If steroids and other hay fever treatments do not work, the GP may refer you for immunotherapy. Did you know that having sex *might* be able to alleviate some of those nasty hay fever symptoms? Back in 2009, a study found a link between sex and a reduction of hay fever symptoms, with Sina Zarrintan, from Tabriz University in Iran, noting that an orgasm might help to decrease nasal congestion. The truth is, the jury is out on whether or not sex can really help hay fever sufferers. Dr Gareth Nye, senior lecturer at Chester Medical School, has doubts about the claim that the redirection of blood from the nose to the genitals would have any effect on hay fever. He does acknowledge that you could experience some relief from symptoms thanks to sex – but not for the reasons you might think. Instead, relief from pain and discomfort could arise from the ‘surge of endorphins that comes from having sex’. That relief won’t last long, though… ‘With the average length of intercourse being around five minutes, you won’t get relief from hay fever for very long, if it does in fact work,’ notes Dr Gareth. And in fact, he adds: ‘If anything, your symptoms may worsen after sexual intercourse, because if blood is being drawn away from the nose there is less immune system presence to control the allergens. ‘When it returns it will work harder to make up for the short fall. ‘We see this when people use decongestants for a long period of time; often you get a brief relief but long term it doesn’t necessarily help.’ We’re not suggesting that you don’t bother having sex – if you’re in the mood, go for it. But if you’re expecting it to serve as a magical remedy for your itchy nose and streaming eyes, you might be disappointed. If you're suffering from allergies, Dr Nye recommends: •Plenty of fluids to keep any excess mucus thin and runny to help clear your nose quicker  •Saline sprays can clear allergens from the nasal cavity •Vasaline around the nostrils will trap much of the pollen •Showering/changing clothes to stop local pollen collections on your person  #CapCut #frontpage #foryou #interesting #trend #foryoupage #trending #funny #meme #hayfever #pollen #health #medicine #medine #facts #LearnOnTikTok #laugh #learnwithtiktok #tiktok #tiktokindia

Access refusals due to allergies.  A big reason teams get refused access to establishments and taxis is due to dog allergies.  Around 8-12% of uk adults have a dog sensitivity. The allergic reaction is to the proteins found in the dogs skin/coat, saliva and urine. Signs of a pet allergy include common hayfever symptoms such as sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose. More serious reactions can include wheezing, hives and difficulty breathing. Full Anaphylaxis is rare in a dog allergy but can happen.  Often unless diagnosed what people think is a dog allergy can actually be an environmental allergy to pollen or dust. These allergens often are at an increase when pets are in the home. Cat allergies are around 50% more common than dog allergies!  Can an establishment refuse access on the premise that someone ‘may’ have an allergy? -No. In the eyes of the law this is not considered a reasonable response.  If someone however is allergic accomodations can still be explored. Non dog allergic staff should be utilised, seperate spaces, asking the handler if the dog could wear a shed defender (they can refuse) or use of cleaning measures are all examples of reasonable adjustments.  #accessrefusal #assistancedogintraining #assistancedoguk #assistancedogsoftiktok #servicedogintraining #servicedogsoftiktok #servicedog #dogsofttiktok #assistancedoglife #allergies #dogallergy #dogallergies #allergy #adjustments #fypシ゚viral #fypage

Toxaprevent mops up histamine and removes it from the body. (Videos available on our YouTube channel - link in bio👀👆) The role of histamine receptors 👇👀 H1R = skin, muscles, heart and central nervous system. When triggered, it is known for allergies such as blocked nose, itchy eyes, urticaria and feeling anxious  H2R = located in the digestive tract is responsible for acid regulation. When triggered, it increases stomach acid to aid in digestion H3R = part of cognitive function. It helps with our sleep-wake cycle, fight and flight and emotions such as pleasure and even regret! H4R = plays a major role in regulating our immune system. And inflammation supporting white blood cells in fighting infection. It is also linked with joint inflammation. The antihistamines designed for histamine receptors: H1R = Cetirizine, Loratadine & Fexofenadine  H2R = Famotidine  H3R = Pitolisant (US Only) H4R = No drug known… yet👀 (JNJ7777120) The better you understand histamine, the more you can reverse your symptoms!  #allergies #allergicreaction #hayfever #histamine
