Growing up, no one ever mentioned allergy anxiety to me. The anxiety, however, stems from trying to keep yourself safe. I never really experienced allergy anxiety until I moved to London when I was around 23 or 24 years old! I think my anxiety came from constantly thinking about my allergy, especially when starting my may contain page it became a more apparent. I became so consumed with creating allergy content that it drove me to a difficult place. I eventually took a six-month break from focusing on may contain so didn’t have to think about creating content. If you've just started an allergy page, this is something to be aware of. I wouldn't want to contribute to worsening someone's anxiety. It's important to take breaks if you feel your anxiety worsening. Take some time away from social media or creating content. I've muted some Instagram accounts that I felt were increasing my anxiety, and this has been helpful.Reading and hearing allergy content all the time isn't always beneficial. It can make you overthink and worsen your anxiety. Traveling has given me a lot of time to reflect and think about my anxiety. I definitely still struggle with it, but I feel like I will be more in control when I come back to the UK.Every time I feel anxiety coming on, I go through a checklist: Are my lips swelling? Do I see hives? Is my breathing okay? In 99% of cases, I don't have any symptoms. Getting fresh air is also important and has helped tremendously. So has being able to talk to someone.  If I were doing this trip solo, I would really struggle without a support system. Being able to ask my partner, "Is my neck red? Can you see hives?" has helped me massively because I know I'm not alone. This post is quite lengthy, but I hope it helps someone who has an allergy and suffers from allergy anxiety. You are not alone. If do need to seek more professional guidance on allergy anxiety please reach out to Allergy UK and Anaphylaxis UK.  If you did find this post has been helpful please share or forward it with your friends and family.  Dan #anxiety #allergy #foodallergy #allergyfriendly #peanutallergy #anxietyrelief

Hayfever is the same as any allergy: your immune system identifies a foreign substance and  to remove it - (pollen )  while “defending” your body from the pollen, your immune system triggers numerous cold-like symptoms that range from frequent sneezing and coughing to severe exhaustion and sickness. Other common hayfever symptoms include : -Runny nose or blocked nose  Red watery eyes  - Itchy throat , Mouth, Nose, Eyes or ears  - Headaches  -Wheezing  - Tight chest  - Loss of smell  Antihistamine tablets , Nasal sprays and eye drops are available on prescription and over the counter to treat the symptoms of hayfever. However, around two thirds of sufferers find their symptoms do not respond to these treatments, and this is where the hayfever injection comes in.  This treatment is highly recommended to have before symptoms arrive to stop the symptoms becoming worse during high pollen count days . Proteins do NOT stay in your breastmilk for weeks! Take diary for example as this is the most common allergen infants react to ( doesnt mean that it is common though, that all babies react to it or that its not another allergen/ protein that they’re reacting to!)   That dairy protein will peak in concentration in your breastmilk around 1 hour maybe 2 after you have eaten/ ingested it. But after 24 hours its GONE! Proteins don’t hang around in your breastmilk for weeks!! Were you told its in there for ages? #allergy #cmpa #baby #breastfeeding

Access refusals due to allergies.  A big reason teams get refused access to establishments and taxis is due to dog allergies.  Around 8-12% of uk adults have a dog sensitivity. The allergic reaction is to the proteins found in the dogs skin/coat, saliva and urine. Signs of a pet allergy include common hayfever symptoms such as sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose. More serious reactions can include wheezing, hives and difficulty breathing. Full Anaphylaxis is rare in a dog allergy but can happen.  Often unless diagnosed what people think is a dog allergy can actually be an environmental allergy to pollen or dust. These allergens often are at an increase when pets are in the home. Cat allergies are around 50% more common than dog allergies!  Can an establishment refuse access on the premise that someone ‘may’ have an allergy? -No. In the eyes of the law this is not considered a reasonable response.  If someone however is allergic accomodations can still be explored. Non dog allergic staff should be utilised, seperate spaces, asking the handler if the dog could wear a shed defender (they can refuse) or use of cleaning measures are all examples of reasonable adjustments.  #accessrefusal #assistancedogintraining #assistancedoguk #assistancedogsoftiktok #servicedogintraining #servicedogsoftiktok #servicedog #dogsofttiktok #assistancedoglife #allergies #dogallergy #dogallergies #allergy #adjustments #fypシ゚viral #fypage

Hayfever injections, also known as allergy shots, are a form of immunotherapy used to treat allergic rhinitis (hayfever) caused by allergens such as pollen, dust mites, pet dander, or mold. These injections work by gradually desensitizing the immune system to specific allergens, reducing the severity of allergic reactions over time. 🌼🤧 Spring Allergy Tips from Your General Practice Physician Associate 🌼🤧 As the flowers bloom and the pollen counts rise, many of you might be starting to feel the seasonal sniffles and sneezes of hay fever. Here are some top tips to help you manage these symptoms: 1. Keep Windows Closed: It might be tempting to let in the fresh spring air, but keeping windows closed can prevent pollen from entering your home and aggravating your allergies. 2. Pollen Forecast: Stay ahead of the game by checking the daily pollen forecast. Try to stay indoors when the pollen count is high, typically on dry, warm, and windy days. 3. Change and Wash Clothes: After being outside, change your clothes and shower to rinse pollen from your skin and hair. 4. Medication: Over-the-counter antihistamines (like Fexofenadine 120mg) can be a game-changer. If you're unsure which is right for you, don't hesitate to ask at the surgery. For persistent symptoms, consider speaking to your GP or physician associate about other options like nasal sprays or eye drops. 5. Wear Sunglasses: A simple pair of sunglasses can help protect your eyes from pollen, reducing itchiness and discomfort. Remember, you're not alone in this! Many people experience hay fever, and we're here to help. If you have any concerns about your symptoms or treatments, please reach out to your GPs/PA/ANP Stay well and enjoy the beauty of spring safely! #HayFeverHelp #SpringAllergies #HealthTips #allergyfriendly #allergyawareness #allergyseason #allergyrelief #hayfever #PhysicianassociateAdvice #physicianassociatestudent #seasonalallergies  #physicianAssociate #GeneralPracticePA

⭐️Food Allergy Awareness Week 22nd-28th April⭐️ Many of you will know about my allergy to Rapeseed Oil. Thousands of people are affected by this allergy, and it can be life threatening. I have to carry an epipen with me due to severe reactions even being near rapeseed in the atmosphere whether it’s in fields, or being used for cooking in restaurants… so it’s not just consuming this oil through food. It should be a recognised allergy, like so many others, but it isn’t. It makes going out to restaurants, grocery shopping, and so much more virtually impossible to do. When you go out for food, and ask to about rapeseed, they can’t often tell you due to it not being in the allergy menu, or so many just say “vegetable oil”, which could be number of different oils! But you can’t take the risk. Rapeseed Oil is in circa 98% of processed food here in the UK. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) says in their Rapid Risk Assessment of Rapeseed Oil that as long as the Erucic acid content doesn't exceed 2% in our food and less in baby formula and baby food, the risk is inconsequential. What the FSA doesn't appear to have considered is that if Rapeseed Oil is in practically every processed food item, take-away meals, and restaurant meals (and not just food but toiletries, cosmetics, supplements, medication, etc) that the build-up levels of Erucic acid being ingested by humans must be much higher than the so-called "safe"level!   Because of this when there are suddenly changes in the use of oils due to supply shortages (eg in crisps) they are not required to update their ingredients lists, making those who suffer with this allergy literally gamble with their life when it comes to consuming food.  Please sign the petition on the link below to identify Rapeseed Oil as a major allergen so that the thousands of us who now suffer allergic reactions to this substance can avoid it and safely consume food.  https://chng.it/XwY84hjcVG #allergy #allergyawareness #rapeseed #rapeseedallergy #allergicreaction #rapeseedoil #petition #fyp #foryou #foryoupage

My Top 7 Suggestions 👇 1) 🌬️An Air Purifier is simple and effective. Especially if, during the heat, you struggle with keeping the windows closed. This can help clean the pollen out of the air. However, make sure you are changing the filters regularly! My favourite is from Amazon (link in bio).  2)☁️ A Humidifier! Yes, a humidifier can help put moisture in the air and help with a blocked nose. We tend to add a drop of eucalyptus or rosemary for a lovely evening aroma. (Link in bio) 3)🍵 Nettle Tea is a natural antihistamine which has been found to block histamine receptors.  4)🐄 Cut out Dairy!! Hay fever sufferers should be aware of dairy (even alternatives) as this can encourage mucous production, worsening symptoms like a blocked nose and a runny nose. This is because as we breathe in the pollen, it attaches to the mucous and continues to trigger histamine symptoms. So, while hay fever season is in full swing, avoiding milk, yoghurt, and even cheese may be best. 5)🥛Take Toxaprevent Daily! Toxaprevent is a histamine binder that mops up and reduces histamine in the body. We recommend starting with the Toxaprevent Medi Plus Sachets (the purple one), as they work in the Upper GI (Mouth, Throat, and Stomach). The link is in my bio! 👈 6) 🛀 Wash your face immediately when getting in from being outside. Pollen can and will attach to your skin. Having a shower is even better as it will clear the pollen and ensure that your histamine 1 receptor isn’t being triggered!  7) 👔 Change clothes when you get in from the outside. Pollen attaches to clothes, and even putting bed linen outside during pollen season can ensure you get those pesky hay fever symptoms as you sleep!  Do you have any tips? Lash Addicts…the dreaded hayfever season has arrived 😭 ▫️If Hayfever affects your eyes making them watery and puffy, you may find this affects lash extension retention  ▫️Watery eyes can affect how well the adhesive cures and may stop it from working properly. ▫️Using eye drops to help with your hayfever can also affect lash extension retention.   ▫️Hayfever is an allergy which could lead to your immune system being weakened. This could potentially mean that even if you have been a lash wearer for years with the same tech and products, you could still develop a reaction or become more sensitive to the adhesive.    DO… ▫️Clean, clean and clean again!! Pollen can sit on the lash extensions heightening the irritation to your eyes. Keeping your lash extensions clean using a lash shampoo daily can help to avoid this. ▫️If you suffer badly from hayfever especially in your eyes..consider taking a lash break during the peak hayfever period. A Lash Lift and Tint would be the perfect alternative during this period!  ▫️Take an antihistamine daily but especially the morning of your lash appointment.  DON’T.. ▫️Rub your eyes. Easier said than done I know!! By rubbing your eyes you will make the irritation worse and risk pulling out your lash extensions therefore affecting the natural lashes.  ▫️Avoid pulling the lash extensions. When your eyes are irritated, it is very easy to find yourself automatically pulling at your lashes. To prevent this..use a cool, slightly damp cloth over your lashes until the irritation eases.  TOP TIP… If you feel the need to itch your eyes, gently use your lash comb to brush your lashes - this will help to ease the itch without harming your lashes. It will also help to remove dirt and pollen caught in your lashes!  #lashesoftiktok #hayfever #lashaddict

Sadly, many time I have started chatting to parents about their babies allergy results and they are so confused.  Yesterday, I called a mum who had been told to avoid wheat, egg, peanuts, hazelnuts, pistachio, soya and milk based on positive IgE blood results. On chatting her baby was tolerating soya, wheat and a small amount of baked egg without concern. So what did I do, ask her to remove it because she had a positive IgE blood result...nope!  Blood results on their own may not mean you have to avoid a food. We have something called false positive and if the number is low your baby may be fine with that food and you don't need to avoid.  However, symptom history is crucial. If there is any symptoms of swelling then this is not advised. Also the number of the result is also crucial. This will all be interpreted by your allergy team so it's so important not to go it alone.  just ask me if worried.  *disclaimer, this is for information purpose only* #allergy #expertadvice #allergyawareness #milkallergy #dietitiansoftiktok

Here are some ways to help manage hay fever -  🤧Medications: Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, nasal sprays, and eye drops can help alleviate symptoms. 🌸Avoid Triggers: Try to stay indoors when pollen counts are high, especially on windy days. Keep windows closed during peak pollen seasons. 👃Nasal Irrigation: Use a saline nasal rinse to flush out pollen and irritants from your nasal passages. 🤧Allergen-proof your home: Keep windows closed, use air purifiers, and regularly clean floors and surfaces to reduce pollen and other allergens indoors. 😷Wear a mask: When doing outdoor activities like gardening, wearing a mask can help filter out pollen and prevent it from entering your airways. 🌸Limit outdoor activities: If possible, avoid outdoor activities during high pollen times, such as early morning and evening. 💦Stay hydrated: Drinking plenty of water can help thin mucus and reduce congestion. 👗Wash after being outdoors: Shower and change clothes after spending time outdoors to remove pollen from your body and clothes. #fyp #pharmacy #HayFever #pharmacytiktok

How to reduce hay fever symptoms  Hay fever is as a result of your immune system reacting to pollen. Pollen is the highest when it’s a warm, humid and windy day. If you can reduce your pollen exposure, your symptoms will be reduced as well.  Here are some practical tips: 1. keep windows and doors shut as much as possible 2. change your clothes after you have been outside - this will help reduce the amount of pollen coming into your house  3. do not cut grass or walk on grass 4. do not dry clothes outside as pollen can settle on them  #hayfever #hayfeverseason #healthylifestyle #healthtips #doctor #fyp

Why were kids that drink RAW DAIRY 59% less likely to get allergies? Because raw milk is REAL milk. Why? Raw milk contains all the peptides, enzymes and good bacteria (to re-populate the gut). Pasteurisation destroys all this. Yes- there’s pros and cons for all types of milk, and some people warn against raw milk bc “they know someone that knows someone who got food poisoning from it” . But did you know you’re 5x more likely to get food poisoning from chicken? So don’t be afraid of dairy, real, raw and unpasteurised A2 milk is amazing for your health. It contains ALL of its natural enzymes, good bacteria, fatty acids, vitamins & minerals. Plus, a proper raw milk producer knows what their doing (they test the cows regularly for any diseases that could affect the milk). Also, if you have lactose issues you should know that the natural enzymes in raw milk actually help you break down lactose, (making it way easier to digest and much better for your metabolism). So even if you struggle to digest conventional dairy – try raw A2 milk, you might be pleasantly surprised. My favourite UK brand of raw A2 milk is @hillfarmrealfood And yes, there are no plant-based suggestions here because I don’t think (most of them) are healthy. If you want to know more about plant-based milks, check out my reel about Oat Milk. But I’m interested, what milk do you drink? Share in the comments below. ⭐️Food Allergy Awareness Week 22nd-28th April⭐️ Many of you will know about my allergy to Rapeseed Oil. Thousands of people are affected by this allergy, and it can be life threatening. I have to carry an epipen with me due to severe reactions even being near rapeseed in the atmosphere whether it’s in fields, or being used for cooking in restaurants… so it’s not just consuming this oil through food. It should be a recognised allergy, like so many others, but it isn’t. It makes going out to restaurants, grocery shopping, and so much more virtually impossible to do. When you go out for food, and ask to about rapeseed, they can’t often tell you due to it not being in the allergy menu, or so many just say “vegetable oil”, which could be number of different oils! But you can’t take the risk. Rapeseed Oil is in circa 98% of processed food here in the UK. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) says in their Rapid Risk Assessment of Rapeseed Oil that as long as the Erucic acid content doesn't exceed 2% in our food and less in baby formula and baby food, the risk is inconsequential. What the FSA doesn't appear to have considered is that if Rapeseed Oil is in practically every processed food item, take-away meals, and restaurant meals (and not just food but toiletries, cosmetics, supplements, medication, etc) that the build-up levels of Erucic acid being ingested by humans must be much higher than the so-called "safe"level!   Because of this when there are suddenly changes in the use of oils due to supply shortages (eg in crisps) they are not required to update their ingredients lists, making those who suffer with this allergy literally gamble with their life when it comes to consuming food.  Please sign the petition on the link below to identify Rapeseed Oil as a major allergen so that the thousands of us who now suffer allergic reactions to this substance can avoid it and safely consume food.  https://chng.it/XwY84hjcVG #allergy #allergyawareness #rapeseed #rapeseedallergy #allergicreaction #rapeseedoil #petition #fyp #foryou #foryoupage

Foraging for nettle leaf tea 🍃 Nettle tea offers several health benefits. Here are some key points about its health benefits and how to make it: 1. Anti-Inflammatory Properties: Nettle tea is known for its anti-inflammatory effects, which can help reduce symptoms of arthritis and other inflammatory conditions. 2. Rich in Nutrient: Nettle leaves are packed with vitamins A, C, K, and several B vitamins, as well as minerals like iron, calcium, magnesium, and potassium. 3. Allergy Relief: Nettle tea may help alleviate symptoms of hay fever and other allergic reactions by acting as a natural antihistamine. 6. Digestive Health: Nettle tea can aid digestion and soothe the gastrointestinal tract, potentially relieving symptoms of IBS and other digestive disorders. 7. Skin Health: Its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties can support skin health, helping to manage conditions like eczema and acne. How to Make Nettle Leaf Tea When foraging nettles yourself, be sure to use gloves to avoid the plant's sting. Here's a simple recipe using the ratio you provided: Ingredients - 1 cup fresh nettle leaves - 2 cups water Instructions 1. Collect fresh nettle leaves from a clean, pesticide-free area. Wear gloves to avoid stings. 2. Rinse the nettle leaves thoroughly to remove any dirt or insects. 3. Bring 2 cups of water to a boil. 4. Once the water is boiling, add the 1 cup of fresh nettle leaves to the pot. 5. Reduce the heat and let the nettles simmer in the water for 10 minutes. 6. After simmering, remove the pot from heat and strain the tea to remove the nettle leaves. 7. Pour the strained tea into a cup. You can drink it hot or let it cool. Add honey or lemon for extra flavor if desired. This basic method ensures you get a flavorful and nutritious nettle tea. Remember to use fresh, young leaves for the best taste and nutritional benefits. #nettletea #foraging #foragingtiktok #skintok #hayfever #fyp

Gut health matters.  Did you know that some microbes produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFA)? These key short chain fatty acids are  - butyrate - propionate - acetate SCFA are vital players in metabolic health as well as in gut health. Certain microbes produce these SCFA which can also go onto feed other ‘good’ microbes in the gut. A reduction in these SFCA can lead to skin issues, breathing issues, allergies, ulcerative colitis, diabetes, cardiovascular health issues etc.  At the New School of Nutritional Medicine, we teach our students on how to get their gut microbiome vibing at a healthier frequency. We implement the comprehensive gut test into our year 1 curriculum as we teach the digestive system. We dive into the gut markers such as pancreatic sufficiency, gut immune health, gall bladder health as well as the microbiome diversity. Dairy free Crispy Garlic Chicken 🤍✨🍴(df and gf) We are back BABY, sorry for the radio silence but we have all of the dairy free summer dishes coming your way!  This recipe is super quick and easy and is SO tasty, we loved serving it with a salad 😍 Serves 4 Ingredients: @Tesco  6 chicken thighs (one pack)  3-5 potatoes (we used red ones)  2-3 parsnips  Dairy free butter  1 tbsp dried parsley, garlic, salt and pepper to season Method: 1. Preheat the oven to 200 degrees 2. Chop the potatoes into cubes and place into oven proof dish 3. Peel and chop the parsnips and place into the same dish 4. Add a few knobs of butter and season well 5. Put a few tablespoons of cornflour onto a plate and coat the chicken thighs 6. Place the chicken thighs onto a hot pan on the stove and add a few knobs of butter, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper  7. Once it is cooked on the outside and coated in the sauce place the chicken on top of the parsnips and potatoes and place into the oven for 30-45 minutes  8. After 30-45 minutes your chicken, potatoes and parsnips should be all cooked and crispy (leave in longer if you want it more crispy)!  Let us know if you try it!! Dairy free Slow Cooker Harissa Chicken 🤍✨🍴(df and gf) We are obsessed with the slow cooker at the moment and makes it so easy as you just throw it all in there and 3 hours later you have a tasty dinner!  Serves 4 Ingredients: @Tesco  4-5 chicken breasts  250ml Elmlea double 100% plant cream  2 tbsp @BELAZU (Bel-uh-zoo) rose harissa paste 😍 200ml chicken stock  1 bag of spinach  1 punnet of mushrooms  1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp of water  1tbsp oregano, garlic and paprika  salt and pepper to season  Method: 1. Cut your chicken breasts into halves and then place in a frying pan to sear the sides for around 10 minutes. Season with paprika, garlic, oregano and salt and pepper.  2. Whilst the chicken is cooking chop up the mushrooms into quarters. 3. Make up your chicken stock by pouring boiling water into the stock cube and stirring through.  4. Once the chicken breasts are seared place them into the slow cooker, with the mushrooms and chicken stock.  5. Add 2 tbsp of the star of the show - the rose harissa paste (you could also use green or red pesto). 6. Stir it all through and then add herbs to your choice we added some more oregano.  7. Make up the cornstarch paste by adding 1tbsp of cornstarch with 1tbsp of cold water and mixing it to form a paste and add to the slow cooker.  8. Place the lid on and set to high for 3-4 hours, you could also set at low for 7 hours.  9. In the last 30 minutes add the spinach and cream and stir together and leave the lid off. 10. Serve and enjoy!!  We served ours with Tenderstem broccoli, sweet potato and rosemary bread. Let us know if you try it!! How to reduce hay fever symptoms  Hay fever is as a result of your immune system reacting to pollen. Pollen is the highest when it’s a warm, humid and windy day. If you can reduce your pollen exposure, your symptoms will be reduced as well.  Here are some practical tips: 1. keep windows and doors shut as much as possible 2. change your clothes after you have been outside - this will help reduce the amount of pollen coming into your house  3. do not cut grass or walk on grass 4. do not dry clothes outside as pollen can settle on them  #hayfever #hayfeverseason #healthylifestyle #healthtips #doctor #fyp

What’s the most common allergen to cause hay fever? 🤧 Drum roll 🥁 It’s grass pollen!  Grass pollen is especially effective at causing hay fever symptoms such as sneezing as it relies on the wind to be pollinated, so the pollen is small and light to ensure it can be easily carried away by the wind (and annoyingly easier to breathe in).  Flower pollen on the other hand tends to rely on bees and insects to be pollinated, so the pollen is bigger and heavier, making it not spread as far. 💚 Elderflower Folklore 💚 As with most trees, the Elder tree is rich in its own mythology and ancient lore, and for centuries it has been thought of as terrible bad luck to harm an elder tree or you will risk angering the elder mother. In fact most foragers, farmers, woodsman and rangers will either refuse to cut or harm an elder tree or will make sure to ask permission before picking her fruits or flowers.  If you accidentally harm an elder tree, then there is a rhyme you can repeat to counteract any damage done.  "Elder tree, give me thy wood,  And when I be a tree,  I give you of mine" Many people know of the benefits of the elderberries, but the elderflower is an equally powerful natural medicine. You can easily dry them out and use them as a tea, which can help you with Coughs, colds, and flu's.  It can also help you manage your hay-fever symptoms! This new evidence should give confidence to parents that peanuts although a common allergen food, should be introduced when starting weaning.  There has been a lot of media coverage about #peanutallergy this week so far and following this I understand how parents may be worried to introduce peanuts when weaning. Especially if family history or your child has another allergy.  The stats from the study indicate that avoiding peanuts in your child's diet may lead to allergy. By introducing peanut products authors suggest that this could prevent 'tens of thousands of cases'.  I posted recently about how to introduce peanuts and also have a blog on this  - available on my website. Another interesting part of this study was that it showed when introduced in younger age that even if avoided between 5-6 years protection continued.  How do you feel about giving your little one peanuts?  More information can be found about the study at;  https://www.nih.gov/news-events/news-releases/introducing-peanut-infancy-prevents-peanut-allergy-into-adolescence#:~:text=NIH%20study%20finds%20protection%20lasts,eat%20peanut%20in%20later%20childhood.&text=Feeding%20children%20peanut%20products%20regularly,as%20desired%20for%20many%20years. #peanutallergy #allergyawareness #allergy #foodallergy

Anti Hayfever injections (Kenalog -triamcinolone acetonide) can be used as an intramuscular injection to treat severe hay fever (allergic rhinitis). This use is typically considered when other treatments, such as antihistamines, nasal sprays, or other allergy medications, have not provided sufficient relief.  Kenalog reduces inflammation and suppresses immune system responses, which can significantly alleviate the symptoms of hay fever, such as nasal congestion, sneezing, and itching. 🤧  The effects can last for several weeks to months. Many patients experience significant relief from hay fever symptoms following a Kenalog injection.  ‼️However, it is not a first-line treatment due to potential side effects.‼️ An extensive medical consultation will take place prior to treatment  Kenalog injections can be an effective treatment for severe hay fever, but they must be used judiciously and under medical supervision due to the potential for significant side effects. #hayfever #relief #coughing #itching #sneezing #kenalog #bottoms #up

They Feast On Us 🤢 #bed. High Humidity: Dust mites thrive in environments with high humidity, typically between 70-80%. They absorb water from the air, making moist conditions ideal for their survival and reproduction. Indoor Settings: Common household environments like bedrooms, living rooms, and bathrooms often provide the warmth and moisture that dust mites need. Bedding, upholstered furniture, and carpets are particularly favorable habitats. Nutrient Sources: Human Skin Cells: Dust mites feed primarily on dead skin cells shed by humans and pets. Since people spend a significant amount of time in their homes, especially in their beds, these areas become rich feeding grounds for mites. Other Organic Matter: They also consume other organic materials found in dust, such as pollen, fungi, and bacteria. Allergy Triggers Allergenic Proteins: Fecal Matter and Body Fragments: Dust mites produce waste products and shed body fragments that contain potent allergenic proteins. These proteins can become airborne and inhaled, triggering allergic reactions in sensitive individuals. Enzymes: The enzymes in dust mite feces, such as Der p 1 and Der f 1, break down proteins in human skin cells, aiding digestion. These enzymes are significant allergens #allergy #hygiene

What’s the most common allergen to cause hay fever? 🤧 Drum roll 🥁 It’s grass pollen!  Grass pollen is especially effective at causing hay fever symptoms such as sneezing as it relies on the wind to be pollinated, so the pollen is small and light to ensure it can be easily carried away by the wind (and annoyingly easier to breathe in).  Flower pollen on the other hand tends to rely on bees and insects to be pollinated, so the pollen is bigger and heavier, making it not spread as far. 💚 Elderflower Folklore 💚 As with most trees, the Elder tree is rich in its own mythology and ancient lore, and for centuries it has been thought of as terrible bad luck to harm an elder tree or you will risk angering the elder mother. In fact most foragers, farmers, woodsman and rangers will either refuse to cut or harm an elder tree or will make sure to ask permission before picking her fruits or flowers.  If you accidentally harm an elder tree, then there is a rhyme you can repeat to counteract any damage done.  "Elder tree, give me thy wood,  And when I be a tree,  I give you of mine" Many people know of the benefits of the elderberries, but the elderflower is an equally powerful natural medicine. You can easily dry them out and use them as a tea, which can help you with Coughs, colds, and flu's.  It can also help you manage your hay-fever symptoms! Emotional Effects of Hayfever: Linking Physical Effects to Emotional Responses Hayfever's physical symptoms can have significant emotional impacts. The release of histamines during an allergic reaction causes intense itching and discomfort, affecting nerve endings. This constant irritation leads to feelings of frustration, wearing down emotional resilience, and making daily life feel like a constant battle. Disrupted sleep from nasal congestion leads to fatigue and cognitive strain on the central nervous system. Chronic fatigue causes helplessness, making it hard to stay motivated and positive, resulting in feelings of being overwhelmed and emotionally drained. Chronic hayfever increases stress levels, straining the nervous system. Heightened stress and anxiety worsen symptoms, creating a vicious cycle. The constant stress causes anxiety about future flare-ups, leading to persistent unease and tension. Herbs That Can Help with Hayfever Several herbs can provide relief from hayfever symptoms. Stinging nettle acts as a natural antihistamine, reducing inflammation and allergy symptoms. Peppermint contains menthol, which acts as a natural decongestant and soothes nasal passages. Chamomile, with its anti-inflammatory and antihistamine properties, is effective in reducing allergy symptoms. Elderflower reduces respiratory inflammation and alleviates a runny nose and congestion. Ginger's strong anti-inflammatory properties help reduce hayfever symptoms. Turmeric, containing curcumin, is an excellent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant, alleviating allergy symptoms. Eyebright is traditionally used to treat eye symptoms like redness, itching, and watering. Licorice root soothes irritated respiratory passages with its anti-inflammatory properties. Physical Barriers to Reduce Hayfever Symptoms Implementing physical barriers can also help manage hayfever symptoms. Wearing sunglasses protects the eyes from pollen, reducing redness, itching, and watering. Face masks filter out pollen particles, preventing them from entering the nose and mouth. Long-sleeved clothing minimizes skin exposure to pollen outdoors. Showering after being outdoors removes pollen from the skin and hair, reducing indoor allergen levels. Washing hands and face frequently removes pollen and reduces symptoms, especially before touching the face. Keeping windows and doors closed on high pollen count days prevents pollen from entering the home. Using air purifiers with HEPA filters traps pollen particles, reducing indoor allergens. Drying clothes indoors prevents pollen from sticking to clothes. Applying petroleum jelly or specialized nasal balm inside the nostrils traps pollen, preventing it from reaching the nasal passages. Brushing pets regularly reduces the pollen they bring indoors. Summary Combining these herbal remedies and physical barriers can help manage hayfever symptoms effectively. Tape your mouth for improved health. Chronic mouth breathing can negatively affect the respiratory system and overall health. Inhaling through the mouth introduces unfiltered, poorly humidified air with minimal temperature regulation into the lungs, which in turn can harm the respiratory system. Night-time mouth breathing is connected to a greater incidence of snoring and sleep apnoea.  Unlike the oral cavity, the nasal cavities warm, humidify and filter the inhaled air, which reduces the probability of colds, flu, allergic reactions, hay fever, and irritable coughing. You may look a little kinky going to bed with tape on your mouth, but if you suspect yourself to be a mouth breather (snoring), then giving mouth tape a try could be massively beneficial. ✨Elderflower cordial recipe (Makes about 2 litres) 🌱Ingredients: About 25 elderflower heads Finely grated zest of 3 unwaxed lemons and 1 orange, plus their juice (about 150ml in total) 1kg raw cane sugar 1 heaped tsp citric acid (optional - helpful as a preservative) 🌱Method: Carefully look at the elderflower heads and remove any insects. Place the elderflower heads into a large bowl together with the orange and lemon zest. Bring 1.5 litres water to the boil and pour over the elderflowers and citrus zest. Cover and leave overnight to infuse. Strain the liquid through a piece of muslin and pour into a saucepan. Add the sugar, the lemon and orange juice and the citric acid (if using). Heat gently to dissolve the sugar, then bring to a simmer and cook for a couple of minutes. Use a funnel to pour the hot syrup into sterilised bottles. Want to know one of my many tips for hayfever sufferers...?  Lay OFF the makeup! 👀 Honestly, if you really struggle with it, and get that awful feeling your skin is crawling and your eyes are watering, just give yourself a break, and have a makeup free day. Pollen particles are less likely to cling to mascara or makeup that sits on the skin. Instead, focus on your skincare, SPF and let your skin breathe. It allows you to swill your eyes and face with cool water too, when it all gets a bit much! Yes reducing histamine is possible 👇 Reducing your histamine will help and it will support with your histamine symptoms, and to do this you need a histamine binder = Toxaprevent.  Antihistamines are great at relieving our allergy symptoms. However, the problem is they do NOT get rid of histamine. So, once the antihistamine wears off, symptoms return! As your body is still being triggered by the allergen.  A histamine binder (Toxaprevent) mops up and reduces then excess histamine in the body. Histamine is what is triggering your histamine symptoms.  If you want to learn more about histamine, follow us @nouveau_healthcare where we explain and reveal everything you need to know about histamine.  Remember, histamine isn’t bad but too much histamine can be a problem!  The research 🤓 1) Diesel exhaust particles directly induce activated mast cells to degranulate and increase histamine levels and symptom severity: https://www.jacionline.org/article/S0091-6749(00)54197-9/fulltext 2) Interaction Between Air Pollutants and Pollen Grains: The Role on the Rising Trend in Allergy: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5941124/ #pollen #hayfever #pollution #allergies

This question has bothering me for a while. Why are allergies and hay fever on the rise? We’re seeing people suffering from allergies for longer and much earlier in the year.  In the UK, it’s estimated nearly 1 in 3 people suffer from allergies 👀 Could the rise of planting male trees, which can be easier to “maintain”, be the reason? And could a solution be to plant more female trees?  Share this with someone who suffers from hay fever👇 The pollen season in the UK has traditionally had 3 distinct but overlapping phases: 🌳 March until May, the blossoming of trees such as hazel and birch creates the first wave of symptoms for some pollen allergy sufferers. 🤧  May until July, grass pollen forms the bulk of the UK’s pollen load. 😷 Weed pollen starts in June and can last well into the autumn! Longer and more intense pollen seasons are inbound. This is why we must focus on balancing the immune system and, most importantly, mopping up and removing the excess histamine… both are possible. We are receiving a lot of calls about hay fever.  Hay fever is an allergic reaction to the fine powder that plants produce, called pollen, usually when it comes into contact with your mouth, nose, eyes and throat.   ✔️ put petroleum jelly (such as Vaseline) around your nostrils to trap pollen ✔️ wear wraparound sunglasses, a mask or a wide-brimmed hat to stop pollen getting into your nose and eyes ✔️ shower and change your clothes after you have been outside to wash pollen off ✔️ keep windows and doors shut as much as possible ✔️ vacuum regularly and dust with a damp cloth ✔️ try to use a pollen filter in the air vents of your car, if you have one, and a HEPA filter in your vaccum cleaner #hayfever #pharmacy #gp #doctor #pharmacist #medication #summer #allergy #nhs

The most important lesson I’ve learnt is that you can still travel and see the world even if you have an allergy 🌎 If someone told me a year ago I could travel around South America for 6 months, I wouldn’t believe them. I’ve always felt constricted most my life that I would only see Europe and America and that’s it! I remember at university everyone was going off to Thailand and I remember thinking that would never be me because of my nut allergy 🥜 I even felt that about South America, I thought I would never be able to eat any of the food! If it wasn’t for a few friends going out here too, I don’t think I would have gone myself!  🙏🏻 I’m hoping by sharing my story, I can empower you to travel and see the world too! My allergy page has always been about breaking the stigma and empowering as many people as possible! Nearly at 10,000 followers, feel very lucky to have so many people watching my journey 🤯 It might look like I’m not struggling travelling with an allergy but don’t get me wrong I still suffer with allergy anxiety everyday! I don’t know what the perfect answer is to try and avoid it. I try and not put myself in situations where I feel it will make my allergy anxiety worse.  Thanks again for all your support and following my journey 🇧🇷 #travelling #allergy #foodallergy #southamerica

🌍💔 Heartbreaking reality: Today I walked in on my 7-year-old son, Jess, watching the news about Jack Fowler’s terrifying experience with #anaphylaxis on an airplane. As a parent, it crushed me to see the horror, shock, and empathy on Jess’s face. It made me realize the immense weight this news carries for a young child.  🚫🥛 From the moment Jess could speak, I taught him to always ask, “Has this got milk in it?” before accepting any food. Sadly, he’s seen his parents, ask the same question and then struggle to trust the reply. It breaks my heart that on a 9-hour flight, I had to give him warm jam sandwiches made 10 hours prior because I couldn’t trust the #airline #food to be safe despite them telling me it was. 💔😔 I often question the impact of my constant vigilance and mistrust on Jess’s mental health. But yet again this news reiterates that the world just isn’t equipped to keep him safe, and he can never trust anyone 100%. It’s a heavy burden for a child to bear.  🙏💪 Despite these challenges, I have to remain positive for Jess. We will continue to advocate for better allergy awareness. Our only hope is that with enough noise, we can create a safer world for our loved ones with allergies. Traveling to South America has been the most challenging and rewarding experience of my life! Living in constant fear of having an allergic reaction is tough, especially when dining out while traveling every day. The inner voice asking, ‘Does my neck feel okay? Is it red?’ is a daily struggle, but I’m determined not to let it hinder me and get in the way.  Being present while eating out has been difficult, but it’s something I’m actively working on. Despite the challenges, I’m proud that I didn’t let my allergy prevent me from exploring South America and eating out in over five different countries. I’m not going sugar coat it going to have times when you feel your allergy anxiety can get the best of me however the good times and experiences out weigh any of the moments!  I’ve seen places I never imagined possible while growing up with allergies. Thank you to everyone who has been on this journey with me! I hope my story inspires you to carve your own path and embark on your dream trip! #allergy #travelling #foodallergy #southamerica

Hayfever hacks…. Stinging nettles: By preventing the body from making inflammatory prostaglandins, the sting results in an overall less inflammatory reaction in the body. Urtication, the practice of intentionally flogging yourself with nettle stings, is used as a treatment for inflammatory conditions such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis that has been proven to be effective by clinical studies. It might seem crazy, but applying nettle to arthritic joints will reduce both pain and dependence on medication! Moreover, nettle may inhibit tryptase, an enzyme that is released alongside histamine and which promotes its effects. Inhibiting it is therefore useful in reducing allergic responses. #fyp #hayfever #health #alhamdulillah

Baby led weaning pancakes I love making these they're so quick and easy.  My son is allergic to dairy, soya, and eggs, so this simple recipe is perfect for us.  Only 3 main ingredients are needed: 1 banana  1/4 Cup Plain Flour 1/4 Cup Almond Milk  1/4 tsp Baking Powder Method: - Mash the banana  Mix in the Almond Milk  Add in the flour and baking powder  Give them a good whisk and set aside whilst the pan heats up Lightly grease the pan with oil or butter of choice  Let the pancakes cook for 1-2 minutes before flipping them over, I've found covering them works best.  Allow 10 minutes for the pancakes to cool down and serve with fruit! I like to use squashed blueberries or large strawberries. Recently at a trade show, I encountered a man who was claiming to fix allergy by using what I can only describe as a magic wand.  I questioned this man and when asked he hadn't heard of anaphylaxis, nor did have any knowledge on allergy. I immediately spoke with the organisers and he was quickly removed from the event due the danger he could cause.  Now the organisers of the event had found that he had come in under a guise selling allergen friendly products and then decided to tout this absolute crap! They had no idea and cannot be blamed for this man.  In all seriousness, his information was so dangerous.  I have recently written a blog on allergy testing and what you should be looking for. Not IgG!  Allergy bloods look for IgE antibodies and are only suitable in immediate allergy where a reaction has occurred.  A hair strand test also, absolute rubbish!  We also cannot diagnose an allergy without the full history.  Please make sure you seek out qualified people for advice. ‼️ TW: EYE PULLING ‼️ Guys I’m so sorry about this one 😂😂😂😂 But in the name of transparency, this is the reality of living with severe allergies. My eyes are in a constant state of allergic conjunctivitis, which is an inflammation of the conjunctiva. The conjunctiva is the tissue that covers the inside of eyelids, as well as the white part of the eyeball.  Allergic conjunctivitis is caused by allergens and irritants, such as pollen, dust and mold (3 things I am wildly allergic to).  Symptoms include:  🌻 Intense itching of the eyes and a persistent urge to rub eyes 🌻 Red eyes 🌻 Watery or white, stringy mucus  🌻 Swollen eyelids I realised that not many people experience their inner eyelids peeling (lucky you 😂), so I thought I’d share a snippet into my daily experience with allergies ✨ *sorry about that random shot where it looks like I have dirty fingernails 😩 I just finished oiling my scalp (the girls that get it… GET IT 😂)* #fyp #allergies #allergy #allergicconjunctivitis

These are only a few of the reasons I love faux plants!👇 They're water free!💧 Possibly the best reason is that you don't have to water them at all! This means that if you're a very busy person and don't have the time to water all of your plants, or maybe you're like me and have ADHD and sometimes just have no inclination to, you still get to enjoy nature with little to no effort! They're so de-stressing! 🌴 When I come home from a long day at work and just want to sit down and chill, I get to come home to a lush rainforest in my living room and experience that every day! They'll never die! 🍃 I get to live in a tropical paradise everyday, knowing that these plants will never catch disease, they'll never get under or overwatered and that they'll never dissappear! They're allergy free! 🤧 as someone who suffers from hay-fever, if I had the amount of real flowers in my room as I do artificial ones I wouldn't make it to the end of the week, they're perfect for anyone with an allergy! They're beautiful all year round! 💞 These plants don't need a certain temperature, they don't need certain light levels and they don't need watering, which means no matter what time of year it is they will survive which is absolutely perfect! They're pet safe! 🐕🐈🐒🐰🦎 I have lots of pets and I can tell you my cat loves to curl up behind my artifical palm and sometimes I even let my gecko have a climb up the faux yucca plants! They love it and I'm sure your pets will too! They're instantly aesthetic! 💅 When you put these plants in your house you don't have to wait months or years for them to grow up or for their flowers to bloom, th beauty is there in an instant! Replying to @therajrpatel1  HAYFEVER ALLERGY MEDICATION BEST ANYIHISTAMINE **Summary of Over-the-Counter Oral Antihistamines** **General Function:** Antihistamines are drugs used to alleviate allergy symptoms by blocking the effects of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions that causes symptoms like congestion, itching, and swelling. **Types of Antihistamines:** 1. **First-Generation Antihistamines:**    - **Examples**:  Diphenhydramine, Chlorpheniramine    - **Characteristics**: Cause drowsiness, shorter duration of action, require more frequent dosing.    - **Forms Available**: Tablets, capsules, liquids, topical creams, gels.    - **Common Side Effects**: Drowsiness, dry mouth, headache.    - **Serious Side Effects**: Vision problems, difficulty urinating.    - **Warnings**: Avoid with alcohol, consult a doctor if you have chronic diseases or are taking sedatives. 2. **Second- and Third-Generation Antihistamines:**    - **Examples**: Cetirizine, Loratadine, Fexofenadine    - **Characteristics**: Target specific receptors, less sedating, longer-lasting.    - **Forms Available**: Tablets, capsules, syrups.    - **Common Side Effects**:      - **Cetirizine**: Drowsiness, headache, stomach pain.      - **Loratadine**: Headache, drowsiness.      - **Fexofenadine**: Headache, dizziness, nausea.    - **Serious Side Effects**: Trouble breathing or swallowing, allergic reactions.    - **Warnings**: Consult your doctor regarding interactions with other medications, especially if you have liver, kidney disease, or asthma. **Takeaway:** There are various OTC antihistamines available to treat allergy symptoms. It's important to choose based on individual health conditions, potential side effects, and specific allergy symptoms. Always consult a healthcare provider before starting a new medication to ensure it's safe, especially if you have pre-existing conditions or are taking other medications. Plantain 🌿 Nature's Natural Antihistamine  ✨️  Plantago lanceolata, commonly known as ribwort plantain, is a medicinal herb that has been used traditionally for hay fever. The herb contains several bioactive compounds, including flavonoids, iridoids and tannins, which may have anti-inflammatory and antihistamine properties.  This herb has traditionally been used as a tonic to tone and help repair irritated mucous membranes of the upper respiratory system.  It may reduce symptoms such as nasal congestion and catarrh which are associated with hayfever.    Plantain is also excellent for coughs of all kinds particularly those dry, irritating, hacking coughs that benefit from a cooling, soothing, moistening remedy that can help to expectorate phlegm . Plantain seems to have the knack of drawing towards it things that are stuck, infected or stagnant, so its a great herb for moving congested mucous whether that be in the lungs or sinuses, as well as toning and healing mucous membranes. I think Plantain works well if you have a cough that seems to linger long after the virus has gone. The Allantoin, one of the constituents in Plantain is great for helping that damaged, irritated tissue of the lung and respiratory tract. Plantain’s healing action extends to other systems of the body. Its antibacterial & soothing action mean its a good herb for managing urinary tract infections, clearing the heat from the burning pain of cystitis and it is soothing too. Hay-fever & Plantain 🌿🤧 Nature's Natural Antihistamine ✨️  Plantago lanceolata, commonly known as ribwort plantain, is a medicinal herb that has been used traditionally for hay fever. The herb contains several bioactive compounds, including flavonoids, iridoids and tannins, which may have anti-inflammatory and antihistamine properties.  This herb has traditionally been used as a tonic to tone and help repair irritated mucous membranes of the upper respiratory system.  It may reduce symptoms such as nasal congestion and catarrh which are associated with hayfever.    Plantain is also excellent for coughs of all kinds particularly those dry, irritating, hacking coughs that benefit from a cooling, soothing, moistening remedy that can help to expectorate phlegm . Plantain seems to have the knack of drawing towards it things that are stuck, infected or stagnant, so its a great herb for moving congested mucous whether that be in the lungs or sinuses, as well as toning and healing mucous membranes. I think Plantain works well if you have a cough that seems to linger long after the virus has gone. The Allantoin, one of the constituents in Plantain is great for helping that damaged, irritated tissue of the lung and respiratory tract. Plantain’s healing action extends to other systems of the body. Its antibacterial & soothing action mean its a good herb for managing urinary tract infections, clearing the heat from the burning pain of cystitis and it is soothing too. “I Hate Sleeping Alone” #really. Dust mites are microscopic creatures that thrive in our homes, particularly in places where they can find their primary food source: dead skin cells. These tiny arachnids are most commonly found in bedding, mattresses, upholstered furniture, and carpets—areas that provide an abundant supply of human skin flakes, warmth, and moisture. Feeding Habits: Dust mites feed on the dead skin cells that humans and pets shed. Each night, as we sleep, we shed tiny particles of skin, which accumulate in our beds. Dust mites feast on these skin flakes, making our beds and pillows ideal environments for their sustenance. Their digestive enzymes break down the skin cells, which they then absorb as nourishment. Preference for Moisture: Dust mites thrive in warm, humid environments. They require a certain level of moisture to survive and reproduce, as it helps them maintain their water balance. The humidity produced by our bodies as we sleep—through sweat and breath—creates the perfect humid microclimate in our bedding. This moisture-rich environment supports the dust mites' lifecycle and allows their population to flourish. Lifecycle and Reproduction: Dust mites reproduce rapidly in favorable conditions. A single dust mite can lay up to 100 eggs in its lifetime, leading to large populations in areas where food and moisture are plentiful. The average lifespan of a dust mite is about two to three months, during which they can produce several generations, further increasing their numbers. #allergy #health

My eyes are in a constant state of allergic conjunctivitis, which is an inflammation of the conjunctiva. The conjunctiva is the tissue that covers the inside of eyelids, as well as the white part of the eyeball.  Allergic conjunctivitis is caused by allergens and irritants, such as pollen, dust and mold (3 things I am wildly allergic to).  Symptoms include:  🌻 Intense itching of the eyes and a persistent urge to rub eyes 🌻 Red eyes 🌻 Watery or white, stringy mucus  🌻 Swollen eyelids I realised that not many people experience their inner eyelids peeling (lucky you 😂), so I thought I’d share a snippet into my daily experience with allergies ✨ *sorry about that random shot where it looks like I have dirty fingernails 😩 I just finished oiling my scalp (the girls that get it… GET IT 😂)* #fyp #allergies #allergy #allergicconjunctivitis

⚠️ STOP overpaying for hay fever medication 🤧 If you're buying branded hay fever and allergy meds, or even if you're getting own-brand ones from somewhere like Tesco, Boots or Sainsbury's, you could save SO much money - sometimes up to 96% ‼️ The key is to look for the active ingredient in whatever hay fever medication works for you, and then ditch the expensive versions. The brand of medicine makes no difference to how well it works, and you could go from paying over 40p per tablet to less than 2p – so it's definitely worth it! Just make sure you stick to legit online pharmacies, check the use-by date and look at the non-active ingredients in case you have any other allergies, as the cheaper products don't always contain the same stuff! #shopping #SaveMoney #hayfever #allergies

How i knew my baby had a Dairy intolerance -  First pic- He was weeks old and covered in spots and red blotches, kept being told it was baby acne (i had never seen a baby with this before )  Second pic- His body was costantly covered like this, this wasnt right! How could this just be just excema?! He was so little Last pic- To this day he still has an outbreak if he has dairy  Other sysmtoms he had-  Would not sleep, screamed for hours at night time, not settling Runny / Blocked nose  Projectile vomiting  Spit up after every feed This carried on for 10 months after going back and forth to doctors and health visitor, creams after creams (even steriod cream) gaviscon - was told it was reflux to begin with, but nothing worked, and then tried remedies dor colic. Until i decided to take it upon myself and stop dairy and within a week his skin started to clear. We then were referred to the community dietitian and referred to the hospital for testing. We were told he has a non IEG intolerance as his symptoms werent life threatening, and hopedully he will grow out of it 🤞🏼🙌🏼 Hes now 3 years old and still has flare ups, really hoping by the age of 5 he grows out of it! Its been a journey! Mums instincts are always right!!  #allergy #dairyintolerant #dairyfree #dairyallergy #dairyintolerance #awareness #dairyallergyawareness

Dermatology and allergy doctors' letters are often wildly inaccurate chronicals of your life, littered with errors which have accumulated one upon the other into a mountain of itchy rubble.   It's not actually the doctors fault. It's the product of poor record sharing, especially with you, the patient. Plus appointments that are too long leading to clinicians being overburdened with work.  We always try to correct anything that's inaccurate, in the hope the next person involved in our care might stand a better chance of making the right decisions with us, and for us. THE BEST HAYFEVER TABLET FOR YOU  **Summary of Over-the-Counter Oral Antihistamines** **General Function:** Antihistamines are drugs used to alleviate allergy symptoms by blocking the effects of histamine, a substance released during allergic reactions that causes symptoms like congestion, itching, and swelling. **Types of Antihistamines:** 1. **First-Generation Antihistamines:**    - **Examples**: Diphenhydramine, Chlorpheniramine    - **Characteristics**: Cause drowsiness, shorter duration of action, require more frequent dosing.    - **Forms Available**: Tablets, capsules, liquids, topical creams, gels.    - **Common Side Effects**: Drowsiness, dry mouth, headache.    - **Serious Side Effects**: Vision problems, difficulty urinating.    - **Warnings**: Avoid with alcohol, consult a doctor if you have chronic diseases or are taking sedatives. 2. **Second- and Third-Generation Antihistamines:**    - **Examples**: Cetirizine, Loratadine, Fexofenadine    - **Characteristics**: Target specific receptors, less sedating, longer-lasting.    - **Forms Available**: Tablets, capsules, syrups.    - **Common Side Effects**:      - **Cetirizine**: Drowsiness, headache, stomach pain.      - **Loratadine**: Headache, drowsiness.      - **Fexofenadine**: Headache, dizziness, nausea.    - **Serious Side Effects**: Trouble breathing or swallowing, allergic reactions.    - **Warnings**: Consult your doctor regarding interactions with other medications, especially if you have liver, kidney disease, or asthma. **Takeaway:** There are various OTC antihistamines available to treat allergy symptoms. It's important to choose based on individual health conditions, potential side effects, and specific allergy symptoms. Always consult a healthcare provider before starting a new medication to ensure it's safe, especially if you have pre-existing conditions or are taking other medications. SERIOUS SIDE EFFECTS OF CETIRIZINE FOR ALLERGY Like all medicines, cetirizine can cause side effects, although not everyone gets them. Common side effects The most common side effect of cetirizine is feeling sleepy and tired. This happens in more than 1 in 10 people. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist if this side effect bothers you or does not go away. Other common side effects of cetirizine happen in more than 1 in 100 people. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist if these side effects bother you or do not go away:     headaches     dry mouth     feeling sick (nausea)     feeling dizzy     diarrhoea     sore throat     sneezing or blocked and runny nose Children are more likely to get diarrhoea, sneezing or a blocked and runny nose than adults. Serious side effects It's rare to have a serious side effect with cetirizine. Hay Fever Season - thanks, but no thanks! Hay fever season is in full swing. If you suffer from allergies you may experience symptoms that affect your mouth such as dry mouth, which may increase your risk of cavities and bleeding gums.  At this time of year you need to work a bit harder to balance out this increased risk. What you can do: * Stay hydrated - drink water throughout the day. * Don't skimp on your home care routine - floss/clean between teeth (before brushing) daily. Brush before bedtime and one other time every day. Use a powered or manual toothbrush to clean along the gum line and each surface of every tooth with a fluoride toothpaste (at least 1350ppm). * Chew sugar free gum  between meals to stimulate saliva flow and combat decay causing bacteria. * Seek advise from your pharmacist about managing your allergies. * Visit your dental team regularly. * Take Time out for Teeth with Growing smiles Coaching  Find more tips for healthy summer smiles, book oral health coaching and order products the professionals recommend at GrowingSmiles.co.uk #growingsmilesuk #hayfever #oralhealth #dentaltipsuk #oralhygiene #summersmiles

Our DairyfrEE Roast Potato Salad (serves 4-6) is our new favourite summer side 🍴☀️ It is super easy and can all just be chucked in a bowl and served, it is a real crowd pleaser 😍 Ingredients: - 1 bag of new potatoes  - 3 tbsp of dairy free plain/greek yogurt (we used @Tesco plant chef one) - 3tbsp of dairy free mayonnaise  - 1 packet of spring onions  - salt, pepper, garlic, rosemary and oregano to season  Optional - you could also add some pancetta/crispy bacon if you wanted!!  1. Put your new potatoes on the boil and set your oven to 180 degrees.  2. Once the potatoes are soft drain them and then place on a piece of parchment paper on a baking tray. 3. Spread the potatoes out and then place another piece of parchment paper on top of the potatoes. 4. Use a cup to smash the potatoes until they are nice and flat, it doesn’t matter if they all merge into one. 5. Once smashed drizzle olive oil and season with salt, pepper, garlic, oregano and rosemary. 6. Place in oven for around 30-45 mins until they are at the crispness you desire.  7. Whilst they are crisping up chop up your spring onions.  8. Once they are nice and crispy take the potatoes out of the oven and use a nice to chop them up into smaller sections.  9. Place the chopped crispy potatoes into a bowl and add your Greek yogurt and mayonnaise, season with salt and pepper and mix together.  10. Add the chopped spring onions, mix together (you can add more mayo and yogurt depending on the consistency you would like) 11. Serve and thank us later!! This is def good to know if youre an allergic person! --- A little about fig tree reaction and  phytophotodermatitis; People can have allergic reactions to fig trees. The latex from unripe figs or any part of the tree can irritate the skin and eyes if not removed quickly. This can be an occupational hazard for fig harvesters, packers, food industry workers, and people who use latex to treat skin conditions.  Some people may also react to fig tree sap or pollen, experiencing symptoms like:  Skin irritation  Itching  Respiratory issues  Burning sensation and pain  Itchy erythema  Edema  Blistering and bullae  These symptoms can be caused by furocoumarins in the fig tree's sap, which can cause a condition called phytophotodermatitis.  This reaction can be activated by sunlight and can develop within 24 hours of exposure, peaking in severity up to 72 hours. I am not a doctor. Teen Girl Loses Life After Sip of Costa Coffee #really It is crucial for staff serving food and beverages to be up to date on allergy protocols to ensure the safety and well-being of their customers. Food allergies can cause severe, potentially life-threatening reactions, such as anaphylaxis, in sensitive individuals. Proper knowledge and adherence to allergy protocols are essential in preventing accidental exposure to allergens. Staff need to be trained on identifying common allergens, understanding cross-contamination risks, and accurately communicating ingredient information to customers. They should know how to handle special requests, such as preparing meals in allergen-free environments or substituting ingredients safely. Additionally, knowing the emergency procedures for managing allergic reactions, including how to use an epinephrine auto-injector, is vital. This knowledge can mean the difference between life and death in a crisis. #allergy #story #teen

Hay Fever Season - thanks, but no thanks! Hay fever season is in full swing. If you suffer from allergies you may experience symptoms that affect your mouth such as dry mouth, which may increase your risk of cavities and bleeding gums.  At this time of year you need to work a bit harder to balance out this increased risk. What you can do: * Stay hydrated - drink water throughout the day. * Don't skimp on your home care routine - floss/clean between teeth (before brushing) daily. Brush before bedtime and one other time every day. Use a powered or manual toothbrush to clean along the gum line and each surface of every tooth with a fluoride toothpaste (at least 1350ppm). * Chew sugar free gum  between meals to stimulate saliva flow and combat decay causing bacteria. * Seek advise from your pharmacist about managing your allergies. * Visit your dental team regularly. * Take Time out for Teeth with Growing smiles Coaching  Find more tips for healthy summer smiles, book oral health coaching and order products the professionals recommend at GrowingSmiles.co.uk #growingsmilesuk #hayfever #oralhealth #dentaltipsuk #oralhygiene #summersmiles

Our DairyfrEE Roast Potato Salad (serves 4-6) is our new favourite summer side 🍴☀️ It is super easy and can all just be chucked in a bowl and served, it is a real crowd pleaser 😍 Ingredients: - 1 bag of new potatoes  - 3 tbsp of dairy free plain/greek yogurt (we used @Tesco plant chef one) - 3tbsp of dairy free mayonnaise  - 1 packet of spring onions  - salt, pepper, garlic, rosemary and oregano to season  Optional - you could also add some pancetta/crispy bacon if you wanted!!  1. Put your new potatoes on the boil and set your oven to 180 degrees.  2. Once the potatoes are soft drain them and then place on a piece of parchment paper on a baking tray. 3. Spread the potatoes out and then place another piece of parchment paper on top of the potatoes. 4. Use a cup to smash the potatoes until they are nice and flat, it doesn’t matter if they all merge into one. 5. Once smashed drizzle olive oil and season with salt, pepper, garlic, oregano and rosemary. 6. Place in oven for around 30-45 mins until they are at the crispness you desire.  7. Whilst they are crisping up chop up your spring onions.  8. Once they are nice and crispy take the potatoes out of the oven and use a nice to chop them up into smaller sections.  9. Place the chopped crispy potatoes into a bowl and add your Greek yogurt and mayonnaise, season with salt and pepper and mix together.  10. Add the chopped spring onions, mix together (you can add more mayo and yogurt depending on the consistency you would like) 11. Serve and thank us later!! This is def good to know if youre an allergic person! --- A little about fig tree reaction and  phytophotodermatitis; People can have allergic reactions to fig trees. The latex from unripe figs or any part of the tree can irritate the skin and eyes if not removed quickly. This can be an occupational hazard for fig harvesters, packers, food industry workers, and people who use latex to treat skin conditions.  Some people may also react to fig tree sap or pollen, experiencing symptoms like:  Skin irritation  Itching  Respiratory issues  Burning sensation and pain  Itchy erythema  Edema  Blistering and bullae  These symptoms can be caused by furocoumarins in the fig tree's sap, which can cause a condition called phytophotodermatitis.  This reaction can be activated by sunlight and can develop within 24 hours of exposure, peaking in severity up to 72 hours. I am not a doctor. If you have a reactoon please speak to one! #eczema  #allergy  #allergicreaction  #gardentok  #figtree  #phytophotodermatitis  #photodermatitis  #hives  #urticaria

Coconut despite it's name is not actually a nut.  It's a drupe!! A drupe is a type if fruit with a hard shell and seed. Other drupes can be olives, cherries and peaches.  This is really important if your little one has a nut allergy. They don't need to avoid coconut too.  Coconut can be found generally in milks, oil and also in a lot of skin creams. You may choose coconut milk as an alternative to add to your babies food if avoiding milk.  Coconut allergy is quite rare but that doesn't mean it can't happen. You may find coconut in some infant formula but this  again is very rare due to the small volume  I've got lots of FREE support on food allergy via my website. Wheat allergy although not as common can occur infants and much like milk allergy little ones can grow out of it.  In the US its estimated that around 1% of children have wheat allergy but 2/3rd outgrow by the age of 12  It's important to track symptoms.  Key points  Wheat allergy isn't the same as coeliac disease. If you do suspect that your little one has wheat allergy then speak to your doctor.  If it is suspected they have coeliac disease then they will require a blood test and symptom history to confirm. For some children they may need a gut biopsy. Most important thing is to make sure your little one has gluten in their diet 6 weeks prior to the test. EpiPen Injection Slow Motion #curious The EpiPen, a life-saving auto-injector for treating severe allergic reactions, is significantly more expensive in the U.S. compared to countries with socialized healthcare systems. This price disparity is driven by several key factors: 1. Lack of Price Regulation in the U.S.: In the United States, drug prices are largely determined by pharmaceutical companies and the market, with minimal government regulation. Unlike countries with socialized healthcare systems, where governments negotiate or set drug prices, the U.S. does not have centralized bargaining power to keep costs down. This allows companies to set higher prices, especially for life-saving medications like the EpiPen. 2. Patent and Market Exclusivity: EpiPen’s manufacturer, Mylan (now Viatris), has maintained a strong market presence through patent protections and aggressive tactics to limit competition. Though other companies have tried to produce generic versions, the lack of competition has allowed the company to keep prices high in the U.S. In countries with socialized healthcare, governments often support the introduction of generics to increase competition and reduce prices. 3. Insurance and High Out-of-Pocket Costs: In the U.S., even though many people have health insurance, the cost of an EpiPen can still be prohibitively high due to high co-pays or deductibles. Without universal healthcare, individuals often bear more of the cost burden directly. In countries with socialized healthcare, patients typically receive medications at little or no cost because the government covers the majority of the expense through taxes. #allergy #health #money

Coconut despite it's name is not actually a nut.  It's a drupe!! A drupe is a type if fruit with a hard shell and seed. Other drupes can be olives, cherries and peaches.  This is really important if your little one has a nut allergy. They don't need to avoid coconut too.  Coconut can be found generally in milks, oil and also in a lot of skin creams. You may choose coconut milk as an alternative to add to your babies food if avoiding milk.  Coconut allergy is quite rare but that doesn't mean it can't happen. You may find coconut in some infant formula but this  again is very rare due to the small volume  I've got lots of FREE support on food allergy via my website. THIS MIGHT STING! 🐝 Did you know only female honey bees sting? Worker bees have barbed stingers, so they can only sting once, and it’s usually to defend the hive. People often don't realise the queen bee can also sting, but her stinger isn’t barbed, so she can sting multiple times, although it’s usually only used against other queens. As for drone bees (the males), they don’t have stingers at all! Their one job is to mate with a queen from another colony, and they don’t play a part in defending the hive. Lazy right?! But what about wasps and bumblebees? Unlike honey bees, bumblebees and wasps have smooth stingers, which means they can sting multiple times without losing their stingers or dying in the process. Check out our other video on how to treat stings. If you are stung, watch out for signs of anaphylaxis! If you notice: - Difficulty breathing - Swelling in your throat or face - Rapid heartbeat or dizziness Seek medical help immediately – anaphylaxis can be life-threatening! Want to avoid stings? Keep calm around bees, avoid waving arms, ditch bright clothes, and skip strong perfumes. Bees are essential for pollination and our ecosystem. Understanding their behaviour helps us coexist peacefully. ❤️ Ever been stung by a bee, wasp, or bumblebee? Some antihistamines taken by allergy sufferers can cause weight gain when taken long term. A small study of 268 antihistamine users  showed roughly a 10% increase in weight, BMI, and waist circumference.* It's thought this is because  they block histamine, and histamine has a role in decreasing hunger signals.  Put simply, antihistamines can make you more hungry and sleepy so less active. And some studies even suggest they may impact metabolism. Weight gain is believed to be more of an issue with newer generation antihistamines, like certirizine, desloratidine and fexofenedine. It is SO hard baking Gluten, Egg and dairy free all at once! I keep trying 🤣 here is today's creation for my little man. Cheesy Herby Scones. Yum!  #allergy #allergies #allergylife #toddlermom #moms #allergymom #dairyfree #eggfree #wheatfree #glutenfree #glutenfreerecipes #yum #fyp #fy #toddlerfood #scones #blw #motherhood #cmpa #cmpaawareness #allergyawareness 💙 Ingredients:    • 2 cups gluten-free self-raising flour  • 1/4 tsp salt  • 1/3 cup oil (use a neutral oil like sunflower, vegetable, or olive oil)  • 2/3 cup dairy-free milk (e.g., almond milk, coconut milk)  • 1 tsp lemon juice or vinegar  • 1/2 to 3/4 cup grated dairy-free cheese (optional, for savory scones)  • Optional: herbs or seasonings for extra flavor  Instructions:  • Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.  • Mix dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the gluten-free self-raising flour and salt.  • Add the oil: Pour the oil into the dry ingredients and mix until it resembles wet sand.  • Add cheese and wet ingredients: If using cheese, stir in the grated dairy-free cheese. Then combine the dairy-free milk and lemon juice, and pour into the dry mixture. Stir until the dough just comes together.  • Shape the dough: Lightly flour a surface and shape the dough into a round, about 1 inch thick. Cut out scones using a round cutter.  • Bake: Place the scones on the prepared baking sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden and risen.  • Cool and serve: Let the scones cool slightly before serving.

“But My Nose Keeps Running” #stop The allergic salute is a repetitive gesture where a person, often a child, rubs or wipes their nose upward with the palm of their hand. This motion is commonly seen in individuals suffering from allergies, particularly allergic rhinitis, where frequent itching and congestion prompt them to try to relieve the discomfort. While this action may offer temporary relief, it can lead to several negative effects. Constantly rubbing the nose can cause irritation and redness on the skin, leading to what is called a "transverse nasal crease," a line across the nose that may become permanent over time. Additionally, the allergic salute can worsen nasal congestion by pushing mucus back into the nasal passages, potentially increasing the risk of sinus infections. Moreover, it spreads germs from the hands to the face, which can lead to further infections or illness. To avoid these issues, it’s better to manage allergy symptoms with proper treatments like antihistamines, nasal sprays, or consulting a healthcare professional for more effective solutions. #allergy #nose #skin #interesting

I haven’t posted in a few days as ive had a tough couple of days at work and ive been completely overwhelmed and ive just not had the mental capacity to post. This should have posted on tuesday and its now Thursday, but you know what they say, better late than never.  Life as a teacher with ADHD, autism and other health conditions is a challenge at the best of times, let alone when it all gets on top of me and overwhelms me. I struggle to regulate my emotions and become completely overwhelmed by my thoughts and feelings. Teaching with these conditions is tough I won’t lie, but its so worth it. Don’t ever believe you can’t achieve your goals because its a challenge or you have conditions that make it more difficult. If you want something enough then you will be able to achieve it. Teaching is such a rewarding job, having autism, ADHD and a physical disability wont stop me doing what i love. If anything it helps me to better understand my SEND students and that’s important to me.  WIEIAD 7 weeks + 1 post bypass. I’ve definitely got a far better understanding of how much my body can manage now and my new limits. Its still tough and the rollercoaster journey continues but im glad im riding this rollercoaster. I have good days and bad days but thats to be expected especially after major surgery less than 2 months ago. The weightloss is slow but steady, as long as im losing i am happy. Sometimes i feel disheartened as others lose more than me in less time, but i try to remind myself that everyone is different and this is my journey.  Ive found it a struggle introducing foods again as im so scared of foamies or worse being sick but I know its part of the journey. Its made even more of a challenge due to my autism but i am doing the best i can and thats what matters. Ill go at my own pace and keep putting one step in front of the other.
