“I Eat Avocado Even Though it Upsets Me” #curious Latex-fruit syndrome is an allergic condition in which individuals who are allergic to latex also experience allergic reactions to certain fruits. This cross-reactivity occurs because the proteins found in latex are structurally similar to those present in specific fruits, causing the immune system to mistakenly recognize them as the same allergens. When these individuals come into contact with these fruits, they may experience allergic symptoms that mirror their reactions to latex. Fruits that are commonly associated with latex-fruit syndrome include bananas, avocados, kiwis, chestnuts, papayas, and pineapples. The proteins in these fruits resemble those in natural rubber latex, which can trigger an immune response. For someone with this condition, even eating or handling these fruits can lead to unpleasant or potentially dangerous allergic reactions. The symptoms of latex-fruit syndrome can vary in intensity. Many individuals experience oral allergy syndrome, where they feel itching, swelling, or tingling in the lips, mouth, or throat after consuming the offending fruit. Other symptoms can include gastrointestinal issues such as nausea, vomiting, or stomach cramps, as well as skin reactions like hives or rashes. In more severe cases, the allergic reaction may progress to anaphylaxis, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate medical attention. #allergy #interesting #health

📣 Anaphylaxis Awareness Week is coming soon, and we are prepared with our first content on Anaphylaxis! 👝 What should your Emergency Allergy Pack contain?  - Allergy Plan (https://www.bsaci.org/professional-resources/resources/paediatric-allergy-action-plans/)  - Antihistamine (a long acting, non-drowsy antihistamine such as Ceterizine is recommended over short acting, sedating Chlorphenamine). - Inhaler and spacer (if a previous history of wheeze) - TWO in date adrenaline pens  2️⃣ Why carry two adrenaline pens?  - The device may fail in some way when used (very rare) - It may be used incorrectly, resulting in wasted medication  - There may be a need for an extra dose  - It provides peace of mind  Images obtained and shared with patients’ consent.#paedsallergyuk #allergies #allergy #kidswithallergies #pediatrics #anaphylaxis #anaphylacticshock #aai #epipen

My beautiful baby girl is suspected of suffering with a dairy allergy 😫 she was initially exclusively breastfed but was permanently attached to me and vomiting frequently. Then went to combi feeding and introduced mamia formula which seemed to be making her uncomfortable 🤔 so we gave Kendamil a try...she was still vomiting loads...projectile...after almost every feed. Sometimes she would immediately vomit following a feed, sometimes it could be hours later. She was struggling with tummyache in lots of discomfort and super unsettled, she had the most horrific rash all over her precious little face bless her which would flare up after feeds and look so agitated. The health visitor took one look at her and immediately said dairy allergy...despite the fact id attended hospital with her earlier that week for advice and was told nothing to worry about and sent home. Esti is now on a prescribed formula we are on day 5 of this now...but the photo on here shows the difference in just 2 days...her rash has practically cleared up!!! I am absolutely amazed, I was expecting a very gradual change but this was almost instant. She is much more settled now and slowly slipping into more of a routine with her feeding and sleeping between feeds. I am now dairy free because I do combi feed and although over time she's now slipping away from the breast (which breaks me) it's important I don't pass on any dairy to her via my milk. Even when she stops breast altogether I think I'm going to stick with this lifestyle change as I personally feel a million times better too! I am less bloated, I can snack much more frequently as everything is low calorie so I can munch more often especially as Esti is settling now and allowing me time to eat and drink. I feel healthier and happier. Esti is still being sick but not as much as she was previously, less projectile now too! She still needs infacol to help with wind and soiling nappies but she's much better and much more settled. Hopefully we are on the right path and she continues to grow and thrive. 🌾Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition where the ingestion of gluten—a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye—causes the immune system to attack the lining of the intestine.  🚸For children (and adults) with coeliac disease, strict adherence to a gluten-free diet is essential, and understanding the risks associated with cross-contamination is vital for maintaining health and preventing symptoms. ✖️Cross-contamination is a significant concern for individuals with coeliac disease, as even small amounts of gluten can trigger an immune response and lead to damage in the small intestine. Awareness and careful food handling practices can significantly reduce the risk of unintentional gluten exposure. ❓What are the main sources of Cross-Contamination?  🍟 Food Preparation Areas: Shared cutting boards, utensils, and countertops can harbour gluten from previous food preparations. 🍴Cooking Equipment: Fryers or pans that have been used for gluten-containing foods can contaminate gluten-free foods.  🍛Shared Serving Dishes: Buffet-style meals where gluten-free items are served alongside gluten-containing dishes can lead to cross-contact. ❓How to prevent prevent Cross-Contamination 👩‍🍳Kitchen Practices:  - Use separate utensils, cutting boards, and cookware for gluten-free foods.  - Clean surfaces thoroughly before preparing gluten-free meals.  - Store gluten-free products in separate containers. 👀 Reading Labels: Always check labels for gluten-free certification and warnings about potential cross-contamination (e.g., “may contain traces of gluten”). ℹ️ Dining Out: Inform restaurant staff about the need for gluten-free preparation and ask about their practices to prevent cross-contamination. 👩‍🏫 Education: Educate family members, friends, and caregivers about the importance of avoiding cross-contamination. 🫙Gluten-Free Products: Choose products specifically labeled as gluten-free and made in dedicated gluten-free facilities when possible. #paedsallergyuk #coeliacdisease #allergies #allergy #kidswithallergies #pediatrics #childrenallergies #allergyawareness #foodintolerance #foodallergies #restaurant #glutenfree #glutenfreemenu

“I Eat Avocado Even Though it Upsets Me” #curious Latex-fruit syndrome is an allergic condition in which individuals who are allergic to latex also experience allergic reactions to certain fruits. This cross-reactivity occurs because the proteins found in latex are structurally similar to those present in specific fruits, causing the immune system to mistakenly recognize them as the same allergens. When these individuals come into contact with these fruits, they may experience allergic symptoms that mirror their reactions to latex. Fruits that are commonly associated with latex-fruit syndrome include bananas, avocados, kiwis, chestnuts, papayas, and pineapples. The proteins in these fruits resemble those in natural rubber latex, which can trigger an immune response. For someone with this condition, even eating or handling these fruits can lead to unpleasant or potentially dangerous allergic reactions. The symptoms of latex-fruit syndrome can vary in intensity. Many individuals experience oral allergy syndrome, where they feel itching, swelling, or tingling in the lips, mouth, or throat after consuming the offending fruit. Other symptoms can include gastrointestinal issues such as nausea, vomiting, or stomach cramps, as well as skin reactions like hives or rashes. In more severe cases, the allergic reaction may progress to anaphylaxis, a life-threatening condition that requires immediate medical attention. #allergy #interesting #health

Replying to @drhelenallergy Another life-threatening allergic reaction treated. National news coverage. Hundreds of enquiries. These stories will always be a huge mix of emotions... shocking, inspiring, and in many ways, terrifying. So what happened? An art teacher, Elaine, suddenly experienced life-threatening symptoms after drinking a ginger beer, despite having no known pre-existing allergies. As she lived in a rural area with poor ambulance response times, she called Jason, the Estates Manager, who lives nearby at York House School. Having completed our training course, Jason quickly identified the symptoms of anaphylaxis and drove over to her house with the school’s Anaphylaxis Kitt. He found Elaine on the floor, struggling to breathe, and didn't hesitate to administer an adrenaline pen. In that moment she showed immediate relief, and he knew he'd done the right thing. He quickly drove her to hospital and was credited by doctors with saving her life. This is an absolutely incredible story, that left our entire team in shock when we first heard it. Thankfully, both Elaine and Jason were happy to tell this story to raise awareness around allergic conditions and adrenaline - a huge thank you to Jayne Mccubbin and the BBC for all their help in amplifying this across national news. #fyp #allergy #epipen #startup #founder #school #emergency #education #news #health

Food doesnt cause eczema. Let me explain. Firstly, it’s important to know that eczema and allergies are medically two completely separate conditions. Eczema is a defect in the skin barrier, that is mostly caused by a genetic mutation (researchers have identified mutations in the genes that encode epidermal or epithelial structural proteins, such as FLG and SPINK5, and genes that encode for major elements in the immune system, such as interleukin (IL) 4, IL5, and IL13, which promote allergic inflammation). (PMID 20739029) When eczema is present, it can be irritated by many things, but these don’t CAUSE the genetic mutations. Just think of other chronic and genetic conditions- would we say dairy or a food caused these? This doesnt mean that food can't irritate eczema (but so can so many other things- but thats a different video). This is a clip from 'Beyond the Itch: Understanding Eczema' given by Odette Rodda (Advanced Nurse Specialst in Eczema) and me, Dr Helen Evans-Howells (Medical Doctor, allergy specialist). Your Mum Was Wrong About This #what Dust mites are microscopic creatures that thrive in warm, humid environments, and our beds provide the perfect conditions for their growth. As we sleep, our bodies naturally release heat and moisture through sweating and breathing. On top of that, we constantly shed skin cells, which become a primary food source for dust mites. These conditions—combined with the soft, porous nature of mattresses, pillows, and bedding—create an ideal environment for them to flourish. When we make our beds immediately after waking up, we trap the warmth and moisture accumulated during the night beneath the sheets and blankets. The confined heat and humidity provide dust mites with exactly what they need to survive and multiply. Without proper ventilation, the dampness remains for longer, creating a cozy habitat for them to grow. Over time, this leads to higher concentrations of dust mites, which can exacerbate respiratory conditions such as allergies, asthma, and even eczema. Allowing the bed to air out for a while before making it can help reduce moisture levels, making the environment less hospitable for dust mites. The circulation of fresh air helps evaporate the trapped sweat and reduce the heat, slowing down dust mite reproduction. In contrast, regularly making the bed right after getting up can accelerate the build-up of dust mites, as they thrive in the warm, damp microclimate created by closed-off bedding. #allergy #parasite #bed #sleep

Replying to @drhelenallergy Another life-threatening allergic reaction treated. National news coverage. Hundreds of enquiries. These stories will always be a huge mix of emotions... shocking, inspiring, and in many ways, terrifying. So what happened? An art teacher, Elaine, suddenly experienced life-threatening symptoms after drinking a ginger beer, despite having no known pre-existing allergies. As she lived in a rural area with poor ambulance response times, she called Jason, the Estates Manager, who lives nearby at York House School. Having completed our training course, Jason quickly identified the symptoms of anaphylaxis and drove over to her house with the school’s Anaphylaxis Kitt. He found Elaine on the floor, struggling to breathe, and didn't hesitate to administer an adrenaline pen. In that moment she showed immediate relief, and he knew he'd done the right thing. He quickly drove her to hospital and was credited by doctors with saving her life. This is an absolutely incredible story, that left our entire team in shock when we first heard it. Thankfully, both Elaine and Jason were happy to tell this story to raise awareness around allergic conditions and adrenaline - a huge thank you to Jayne Mccubbin and the BBC for all their help in amplifying this across national news. #fyp #allergy #epipen #startup #founder #school #emergency #education #news #health

As usual, I'm blaming any symptoms on perimenopause.  My latest is dermatitis (as suggested by my GP after I emailed him pics of my inflamed face).  The itching!! 😬😬😬 I had itchy, 'bumpy' skin a few weeks prior which I put down to dryness and the change in season and this episode was remedied fairly swiftly by an epic new moisturiser (Glossier After Baume Moisture Barrier Recovery Cream) in case you're interested).  BUT  I had a flare up two weeks later and this time it was much, much worse: stingy, itchy, red.  I ditched all skincare & makeup products for several days and was even scared to wash my hair. I thought I'd maybe taken an allergic reaction to something but couldn't think what.  The previous weekend I'd had a spray tan (which definitely dries my skin) and was drinking beer (histamine intolerance?). I'd also been for a swim in a pool that seemed extra chlorinated and had a steam room.  The doc prescribed a hydrocortisone cream and I got antihistamines and a heavy duty moisturiser from the pharmacy (with paraffin wax and a scary warning not to go near a naked flame 😕).  Within a few days, the rash disappeared and the itchiness improved but I'm being careful to reintroduce my skincare products slowly so I can see if my skin reacts again.  Honestly, I think it's probably just a combination of all the different factors I've mentioned above - but, crucially, I think fluctuating hormones have made my skin more sensitive.  #skin #sensitiveskin #skinsensitivity #allergy #eczema #dermatitis #flareup

We've been dealing with allergies for almost five years, there is some comfort to think how far we've come in terms of identifying and being able to avoid allergens (with nearly 15 allergens, this felt relentless!), understanding reactions and even the wider landscape in terms of the introduction of Natasha's Law and the increased levels of public awareness etc. Our youngest has more or less outgrown her CMPA allergy which is a big win for us as a family as avoiding dairy and soya along with all of the eldest anaphylactic ones didn't leave us with much to eat as a family! Finally, we have a team of allergy and eczema specialists we feel we can trust so to anyone in the trenches struggling to get anyone to listen, keep going back, keep pushing for referrals. Even the amount of support and resources online has changed significantly, with so much more information out there than when my daughter was first diagnosed. If you are new to allergies or wondering if your child has them, please seek medical advice. #creatorsearchinsights   💔 Saddened by the news of yet another youngwithout life taken too some due to seemingly carelessness around handling of allergens in a restaurant in Italy. It is essential that we are aware of the symptoms of anaphylaxis and we act quickly in the event of experiencing it as it is a medical emergency. Whilst incidents of fatal anaphylaxis are incredibly rare, it is a risk the allergy community are all too aware of nonetheless.  Each time another headline emerges around an allergy death, I personally feel more anxious than ever about my own allergic daughter's future. That's why I started Epicase, to find a way to encourage people with allergies, especially children and young people allergies, especially children and young people who are the most vulnerable, to carry to their EpiPens or other AAl everywhere, all the time. There is more work to be done to making dining out more accessible and safer, and I'm so grateful to Natasha and Owen's families are campaigning for legal changes but there alsofood seems to be a case for ensuring more people have access to the adrenaline treatment forn UK anaphylaxis as soon as possible as this can be incredibly effective at halting anaphylaxis when administered quickly enough. Please note, I do not know of the circumstances of yesterday's tragedy and I am in no way laying any blame with the family here, or in any similar circumstances - people being given food they are allergic to should not happen, period. Sending our thoughts and condolences to the family affected in Rome yesterday. We've been dealing with allergies for almost five years, there is some comfort to think how far we've come in terms of identifying and being able to avoid allergens (with nearly 15 allergens, this felt relentless!), understanding reactions and even the wider landscape in terms of the introduction of Natasha's Law and the increased levels of public awareness etc. Our youngest has more or less outgrown her CMPA allergy which is a big win for us as a family as avoiding dairy and soya along with all of the eldest anaphylactic ones didn't leave us with much to eat as a family! Finally, we have a team of allergy and eczema specialists we feel we can trust so to anyone in the trenches struggling to get anyone to listen, keep going back, keep pushing for referrals. Even the amount of support and resources online has changed significantly, with so much more information out there than when my daughter was first diagnosed. If you are new to allergies or wondering if your child has them, please seek medical advice. This is the partnership we’ve always dreamed of. Kitt Medical x @St John Ambulance England Founded almost 150 years ago, St John Ambulance is England's leading first aid charity - and their endorsement to boost the delivery of emergency allergy treatment and training for schools and qualifying businesses means the world to us. As the market leader of workplace first aid training and supplies, their vision is a world where everyone receives the help they need in a health crisis. With our goal at Kitt being to create a new standard for allergy care, this is truly one of the most validating, exciting, and rewarding moments in our startup journey so far. I can’t tell you the amount of times we had something potentially huge on the horizon, and then it didn’t pan out. Well, this time it did. Together, we’ll improve the quality of life for those living with severe allergies and increase the availability of emergency anaphylaxis treatment. Coming back after a summer hiatus  .  Ive wanted to come back on here and post an  update for such a long time but couldn’t work out why I wanted to do it and what would be the most valuable thing to post both for me and others.  Watching Briana’s amazing documentary on this crazy condition and looking back over the messages I’d been sent over the last year it’s more apparent than ever that the only way to make change. And the only way we can limit and ultimately stop people going through this is to spread as much awareness as possible, about what this condition is, how long it lasts and how the condition affects those who have it.  I don’t have the cure for this condition, I’m still tackling it every day. There’s more good days than bad but ultimately I’m still very much on the journey to recovery. So I will endeavour to be as open and honest about what im going through and what steps im taking to try and heal both mind & body. Huge fucking love to everyone going through this. Time for change  Whilst I know that healing isn’t linear and next week my body may take a turn. Right now things are positive, my body feels strong and that’s it’s healing. My sleep is stable and I’m feeling grateful for every bit of my day that feels normal again.  Having time to reflect on what I’ve been through and thinking about all the other people I speak too regularly I’m determined to spread more awareness about this to help others going through this feel less alone. But also to start a dialogue on how we can make change, to stop others going though this nightmare.  I’m sure there are lots of people already making waves. I’m not here to reinvent the wheel. I’m just offering myself up to be of service to this cause and help to prevent others going through this.  If anyone watching this resonates and have things in the works that they’re working on or has some ideas but hasn’t sat down to put it into action. Please get in touch. Determined to make this wild negative time in my life convert into something positive and make some real change.  Huge love to everyone! This is the partnership we’ve always dreamed of. Kitt Medical x @St John Ambulance England Founded almost 150 years ago, St John Ambulance is England's leading first aid charity - and their endorsement to boost the delivery of emergency allergy treatment and training for schools and qualifying businesses means the world to us. As the market leader of workplace first aid training and supplies, their vision is a world where everyone receives the help they need in a health crisis. With our goal at Kitt being to create a new standard for allergy care, this is truly one of the most validating, exciting, and rewarding moments in our startup journey so far. I can’t tell you the amount of times we had something potentially huge on the horizon, and then it didn’t pan out. Well, this time it did. Together, we’ll improve the quality of life for those living with severe allergies and increase the availability of emergency anaphylaxis treatment. Time for change  Whilst I know that healing isn’t linear and next week my body may take a turn. Right now things are positive, my body feels strong and that’s it’s healing. My sleep is stable and I’m feeling grateful for every bit of my day that feels normal again.  Having time to reflect on what I’ve been through and thinking about all the other people I speak too regularly I’m determined to spread more awareness about this to help others going through this feel less alone. But also to start a dialogue on how we can make change, to stop others going though this nightmare.  I’m sure there are lots of people already making waves. I’m not here to reinvent the wheel. I’m just offering myself up to be of service to this cause and help to prevent others going through this.  If anyone watching this resonates and have things in the works that they’re working on or has some ideas but hasn’t sat down to put it into action. Please get in touch. Determined to make this wild negative time in my life convert into something positive and make some real change.  Huge love to everyone! I haven't stopped thinking about the tragic case of George Cadman-Ithell and his family this week, or any of the allergy tragedies which seem to happen all too often lately. Sadly, it now seems like George may have inadvertently worsened the severity of his reaction by running home during it to retrieve his EpiPens. This is in no way victim blaming but it is clear that many people aren't aware of co-factors such as exercise which can worsen anaphylaxis. Other cofactors include illness, alcohol, asthma and fatigue. But the other key factor is that too many allergy tragedies happen as a result of the victim not having their EpiPen to hand, usually wrongly assuming they have a 'mild' allergy having never suffered extreme reactions before. All people who have been prescribed EpiPens or Jext should ALWAYS carry both of them at all times to ensure they have prompt access to the treatment which is very safe and effective when given. Severe reactions can happen at any time, often when you least expect it. My heart goes out to George and his family, but I am so grateful to his mum for sharing his story to help raise awareness. #allergy #allergyawareness #anaphylaxis #allergymum #allergymom #foodallergy #epipen #allergies #ConSantanderConecto

Adrenaline pens NEED to be used immediately if you’re having a severe allergic reaction. Movement is a co-factor - it worsens symptoms of anaphylaxis like your airway closing up, dizziness, sickness and loss of consciousness. But when George accidentally ate something that contained nuts and realised he didn’t have his pens on him, he ran 8 minutes home. By the time his mum got there, paramedics were desperately trying to resuscitate him. George now lies in a vegetative state in hospital, two months on from his anaphylactic reaction. But as I write this, I’m a huge hypocrite. Just like George, I was diagnosed at 5 years old with severe nut allergies. Just like George, I’ve thankfully never needed to use my adrenaline pens. I normally carry them with me at all times, but when I got home from a long hike and lunch with friends on Saturday, I realised I had gone the entire day without my pens on me. I had a momentary panic before my girlfriend thankfully reminded me I was fine, nothing happened, and I’m home safe. But something could have happened… It’s just too easy to forget something so potentially life-saving. My heart goes out to George, his family, and his friends during this horribly difficult time.
